translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han he was defense commissioner of Yue while also commanding the Left Wing of the Guard Sacred Army, then was posted as defense commissioner of Fu.

sentences.zh: 周祖平內難後，北征契丹，以彥超為行營馬步左廂都排陣使，從周祖入汴。

translations.literal: After the Zhou founder pacified the internal crisis, he marched north against the Khitan; Yanchao was made left-wing horse-and-foot array deployment commander of the campaign headquarters and followed the Zhou founder into Bian.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou founder settled the internal crisis, he marched north against the Khitan; Yanchao was made left-wing horse-and-foot array deployment commander and followed the Zhou founder into Bian.

sentences.zh: 時自彭門迎湘陰公入纘位，會軍變，周祖革命，即命彥超權知徐州節度。

translations.literal: At that time they were welcoming the Duke of Xiangyin from Peng Gate to succeed to the throne; an army mutiny occurred, the Zhou founder seized power, and Yanchao was immediately ordered to serve as acting military governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were bringing the Duke of Xiangyin from Peng Gate to succeed to the throne; when the army mutinied and the Zhou founder seized power, Yanchao was immediately made acting military governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，湘陰公舊校鞏廷美據州叛，真拜彥超武寧軍節度，命討之。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Gong Tingmei, an old officer of the Duke of Xiangyin, seized the prefecture and rebelled; Yanchao was formally appointed military governor of the Wuning Army and ordered to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Gong Tingmei, a former officer of the Duke of Xiangyin, seized the prefecture and rebelled; Yanchao was formally appointed Wuning military governor and ordered to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 彥超督戰艦破其水砦，乘勝拔之。

translations.literal: Yanchao directed the war vessels, broke their water fort, and seized victory to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao directed the war vessels, broke their river fort, and took it in the rout.

sentences.zh: 又與樞密使王峻拒劉崇於晉州，彥超以騎兵進，崇遁去，授建雄軍節度。

translations.literal: He also joined Grand Councilor Wang Jun in resisting Liu Chong at Jin Prefecture; Yanchao advanced with cavalry, Chong fled, and Yanchao was granted the Jianxiong military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Grand Councilor Wang Jun in holding Liu Chong at Jin; Yanchao advanced with cavalry, Chong fled, and Yanchao was made military governor of Jianxiong.

sentences.zh: 復以所部追賊至霍邑，賊步騎墮崖谷，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Again with his own troops he pursued the enemy to Huoyi; enemy foot soldiers and cavalry fell into cliff ravines, and the dead were extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the enemy with his own troops as far as Huoyi; foot soldiers and cavalry tumbled into ravines, and casualties were heavy.

sentences.zh: 彥超歸鎮所，俄改河陽三城節度，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: Yanchao returned to his garrison post; shortly thereafter he was changed to military governor of the Heyang Three Cities and transferred to govern Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao returned to his post, was soon made governor of the Heyang Three Cities, and then transferred to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was given the additional title of Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande he was made Tongpingzhangshi.

sentences.zh: 劉崇南寇，命彥超領兵取晉州路東向邀擊，從戰高平。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong raided southward, Yanchao was ordered to lead troops by the Jin Prefecture route to intercept from the east and took part in the battle at Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong raided southward, Yanchao was ordered to take the Jin route and intercept from the east, and fought at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 彥超自陰地關與符彥卿會兵圍汾州，諸將請急攻，彥超曰：“城已危矣，旦暮將降，我士卒精銳，儻驅以先登，必死傷者眾，少待之。

translations.literal: Yanchao came from Yindi Pass and joined Fu Yanqing in encircling Fen Prefecture; the generals requested an urgent assault, but Yanchao said: "The city is already in peril and will surrender before long. Our soldiers are elite—if we drive them to be first up the wall, casualties will surely be heavy. Wait a little."
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao came through Yindi Pass and joined Fu Yanqing in besieging Fen; when the generals urged an immediate assault, Yanchao said, "The city is already doomed and will surrender soon. Our men are crack troops—if we drive them to scale the walls first, many will die. Wait a little."

sentences.zh: ”翌日，州將董希顏果降。

translations.literal: The next day the prefecture commander Dong Xiyan indeed surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the prefecture commander Dong Xiyan did surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵趣石州，彥超親鼓士乘城，躬冒矢石，數日下之，擒其守將安彥進，獻行在。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops toward Shi Prefecture; Yanchao personally beat the drums to urge the soldiers in scaling the wall, himself exposed to arrows and stones; within several days the city was taken, its defender An Yanjin was captured, and he was presented at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched on Shi; Yanchao beat the drums himself to urge the assault, exposing himself to arrows and stones; within days the city fell, its defender An Yanjin was captured, and he was presented at the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 師還，改忠武軍節度，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was changed to military governor of the Zhongwu Army and additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he was made Zhongwu military governor and also Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 詔率所部浚胡蘆河，城李晏口。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to lead his troops in dredging the Hulus River and fortifying Li Yankou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to dredge the Hulus River and fortify Li Yankou with his troops.

sentences.zh: 工未畢，遼人萬餘騎來侵，彥超擊敗之，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Before the work was finished, more than ten thousand Liao horsemen came to invade; Yanchao defeated them, and the killed and wounded were extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Before the work was finished, more than ten thousand Liao horsemen attacked; Yanchao defeated them with heavy casualties on their side.

sentences.zh: 宰相李穀征淮南，以彥超為前軍行營副部署，敗淮南軍二千於壽州城下。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Li Gu campaigned against Huainan, Yanchao was made deputy commander of the vanguard campaign headquarters and defeated two thousand Huainan troops below the walls of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Li Gu campaigned against Huainan, Yanchao served as deputy commander of the vanguard and routed two thousand Huainan troops beneath the walls of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 吳兵水陸來援，穀退保正陽，吳人躡其後。

translations.literal: Wu troops came to relieve by land and water; Gu retreated to hold Zhengyang, and the Wu forces followed close behind.
translations.idiomatic: Wu troops came to relieve the city by land and water; Gu fell back to Zhengyang with the Wu forces close on his heels.

sentences.zh: 會李重進兵至，合勢急擊，大敗吳人三萬餘眾，追北二十餘里。

translations.literal: When Li Chongjin's troops arrived, they combined forces in a fierce attack and greatly defeated more than thirty thousand Wu troops, pursuing them north for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chongjin arrived, their combined forces struck hard, crushing more than thirty thousand Wu troops and pursuing them north for over twenty li.

sentences.zh: 還，改京兆尹、永興軍節度。

translations.literal: On returning he was changed to Intendant of Jingzhao and military governor of the Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Intendant of Jingzhao and Yongxing military governor.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，移鎮鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year he was transferred to garrison Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year he was transferred to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，加檢校太師、西面緣邊副都部署。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, Yanchao was given the additional titles of honorary Grand Preceptor and deputy overall deployment commander of the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, Yanchao was made honorary Grand Preceptor and deputy overall deployment commander of the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加兼中書令，代還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was additionally made Director of the Chancellery and replaced, returning to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was also made Director of the Chancellery and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖與彥超有舊，因幸作坊，召從臣宴射，酒酣，謂彥超曰：“卿昔在復州，朕往依卿，何不納我？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu and Yanchao had old ties; on one occasion, visiting the workshops, he summoned his ministers to a banquet with archery, and when the wine had gone deep he said to Yanchao: "When you were at Fu Prefecture, I once came to rely on you—why did you not take me in?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Yanchao went back a long way. During a visit to the workshops he summoned his ministers to a banquet with archery, and when the wine was flowing freely he said to Yanchao, "When you were at Fu, I once came to you for shelter. Why didn't you take me in?"

sentences.zh: ”彥超降階頓首曰：“勺水豈能止神龍耶！

translations.literal: Yanchao descended the steps, kowtowed, and said: "Can a spoonful of water stop a divine dragon!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao stepped down, kowtowed, and said, "Can a spoonful of water stop a divine dragon!"

sentences.zh: 當日陛下不留滯於小郡者，蓋天使然爾。

translations.literal: That Your Majesty did not linger in a small prefecture was surely because Heaven willed it so.
translations.idiomatic: That Your Majesty did not remain in some small prefecture was surely Heaven's doing.

sentences.zh: ”帝大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 彥超翌日奉表待罪，帝遣中使慰諭，令赴朝謁。

translations.literal: The next day Yanchao submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; the emperor sent a palace envoy to comfort and instruct him and ordered him to attend court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yanchao submitted a memorial accepting blame; the emperor sent a palace envoy to reassure him and ordered him to attend court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以為永興軍節度。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made military governor of the Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made Yongxing military governor.

sentences.zh: 又以其父光祿卿致仕重霸為太子少傅致仕。

translations.literal: His father Chongba, a retired Guanglu Qing, was also made a retired Crown Prince Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chongba, a retired Guanglu Qing, was also granted retirement as Crown Prince Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，復鎮鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he again garrisoned Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he returned to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 三年，丁外艱，起復。

translations.literal: In the third year he mourned his father's death and was recalled from mourning to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered mourning for his father but was recalled to duty before the period ended.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，為右金吾衛上將軍判街仗事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he served as Right Golden Guard General overseeing street ceremonial duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he served as Right Golden Guard General overseeing street ceremonial duties.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，封邠國公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he was enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he was enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 七年，彥超語人曰：“人臣七十致仕，古之制也。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Yanchao told others: "For a minister to retire at seventy is the ancient regulation."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Yanchao told others, "A minister who reaches seventy should retire—that is the ancient rule."

sentences.zh: 我年六十九，當自知止。

translations.literal: I am sixty-nine; I ought to know when to stop.
translations.idiomatic: I am sixty-nine; I ought to know when to stop.

sentences.zh: ”明年，表求致仕，加太子太師，給金吾上將軍祿。

translations.literal: The next year he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he was given the additional title of Crown Prince Grand Tutor and granted the salary of a Golden Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he requested retirement by memorial; he was made Crown Prince Grand Tutor and granted a Golden Guard General's salary.

sentences.zh: 彥超既得請，盡斥去僕妾之冗食者，居處服用，咸遵儉約。

translations.literal: Once Yanchao had obtained his request, he dismissed all superfluous servants and concubines; in dwelling, dress, and daily use he followed frugal restraint throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Once his retirement was granted, Yanchao dismissed every superfluous servant and concubine and lived in plain frugality in dwelling, dress, and daily use.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書令。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，彥超自鳳翔來朝，與武行德、郭從義、白重讚、楊廷璋俱侍曲宴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao, Yanchao came from Fengxiang to court and, together with Wu Xingde, Guo Congyi, Bai Chongzan, and Yang Tingzhang, attended an informal banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaibao, Yanchao came from Fengxiang to court and, with Wu Xingde, Guo Congyi, Bai Chongzan, and Yang Tingzhang, attended an informal banquet.

sentences.zh: 太祖從容謂曰：“卿等皆國家舊臣，久臨劇鎮，王事鞅掌，非朕所以優賢之意。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu said at ease: "You are all old ministers of the state who have long governed difficult prefectures; royal affairs have kept you overwhelmed—this is not my intent in honoring the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said easily, "You are all veteran ministers who have long governed difficult posts, overwhelmed by state business—this is not how I mean to honor worthy men."

sentences.zh: ”彥超知旨，即前奏曰：“臣無勳勞，久冒榮寵，今已衰朽，願乞骸骨歸丘園，臣之願也。

translations.literal: Yanchao grasped his meaning, stepped forward, and memorialized: "Your servant has no merit to speak of and has long enjoyed undeserved glory and favor; I am now decayed with age and wish to beg my old bones to return to my garden and hills—this is your servant's wish."
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao understood the hint and stepped forward: "I have no merit to speak of and have long enjoyed honors I did not earn. I am old and worn now, and wish only to retire to my garden and hills—that is my wish."

sentences.zh: ”行德等竟自陳夙昔戰功及履歷艱苦，帝曰：“此異代事，何足論？

translations.literal: Xingde and the others, by contrast, each recounted their past battle merits and the hardships of their careers; the emperor said: "These are matters of a different age—what is there to discuss?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingde and the others, by contrast, recounted their old battle honors and the hardships of their careers. The emperor said, "Those are matters of another age—what is there to discuss?"

sentences.zh: ”翌日，皆罷行德等節鎮。

translations.literal: The next day the military governorships of Xingde and the others were all removed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xingde and the others were all removed from their military governorships.

sentences.zh: 時議以此許彥超。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion praised Yanchao for this.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion at the time praised Yanchao for this.

sentences.zh: 張永德

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde

sentences.zh: 張永德，字抱一，并州陽曲人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde, styled Baoyi, was a native of Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde, styled Baoyi, was from Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家世饒財。

translations.literal: His family for generations was wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been wealthy for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖丕，尚氣節。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Pi valued integrity and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Pi was a man of integrity and spirit.

sentences.zh: 後唐武皇鎮太原，急於用度，多嚴選富家子掌帑庫。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor of Later Tang garrisoned Taiyuan and was urgent for funds, he strictly selected sons of wealthy families to manage the treasury and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Martial Emperor of Later Tang held Taiyuan and was hard pressed for funds, he strictly selected sons of wealthy families to manage the treasury.

sentences.zh: 或調度不給，即坐誅，沒入貲寧。

translations.literal: If allocations could not be supplied, they were immediately executed and their assets confiscated to settle accounts.
translations.idiomatic: If supplies ran short, the manager was executed on the spot and his assets confiscated to make up the deficit.

sentences.zh: 丕為之潢滿歲，府財有餘。

translations.literal: Pi managed the accounts for a full year, and the prefectural treasury had a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Pi managed the accounts for a full year and left the prefectural treasury with a surplus.

sentences.zh: 宗人政當次補其任，率族屬泣拜，請丕濟其急，丕又為代掌一年，鄉里服其義。

translations.literal: A clansman named Zheng was next in turn to fill the post; he led the clan in weeping and kowtowing, begging Pi to relieve their emergency, and Pi again substituted and managed for one year; the village and neighborhood admired his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When a clansman named Zheng was next in line for the post, the whole clan came weeping and kowtowing, begging Pi to save them; Pi served another year in Zheng's place, and neighbors admired his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 父穎事晉至安州防禦使。

translations.literal: His father Ying served Jin and rose to defense commissioner of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying served the Jin and rose to defense commissioner of An.

sentences.zh: 永德生四歲，母馬氏被出，育於祖母，事繼母劉以孝聞。

translations.literal: When Yongde was four years old his mother, Lady Ma, was dismissed from the household; he was raised by his grandmother and became renowned for filial service to his stepmother, Lady Liu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongde was four his mother, Lady Ma, was cast out; he was raised by his grandmother and became known for filial devotion to his stepmother, Lady Liu.

sentences.zh: 周祖初為侍衛吏，與穎善，乃以女妻永德。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder was first an officer of the palace guard and was on good terms with Ying, he gave his daughter in marriage to Yongde.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder was still a palace guard officer and friendly with Ying, he gave his daughter to Yongde in marriage.

sentences.zh: 永德迎其母妻詣宋州。

translations.literal: Yongde went to meet his mother and wife and proceeded to Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde went to fetch his mother and wife and proceeded to Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時寇賊充斥，乃易弊衣，毀容儀，居委巷中。

translations.literal: Bandits and robbers filled the region at the time, so he changed into worn clothes, disfigured his appearance, and lived in a back alley.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits filled the region, so he put on ragged clothes, disfigured his appearance, and hid in a back alley.

sentences.zh: 有賊過，即邀乞焉，紿曰：“此悲田院耳。

translations.literal: When bandits passed by he would beg from them, deceiving them by saying: "This is a Compassion Field hospice."
translations.idiomatic: When bandits passed he would beg from them, claiming, "This is a Compassion Field hospice."

sentences.zh: ”賊即舍去，繇是免禍。

translations.literal: The bandits then left, and thereby he escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits passed on, and so he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 周祖為樞密使。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder became Grand Councilor of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder became Grand Councilor of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 表永德授供奉官押班。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Yongde be granted the post of Attendant Official leading the squad.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Yongde for appointment as Attendant Official leading the squad.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，命賜潞帥常遇生辰禮幣。

translations.literal: During Qianyou he was ordered to bestow birthday ceremonial gifts upon Chang Yu, military governor of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou he was ordered to deliver birthday ceremonial gifts to Chang Yu, military governor of Lu.

sentences.zh: 遇，周祖之外兄弟也。

translations.literal: Yu was an outer brother of the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was a cousin of the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 時周祖鎮鄴，被讒，族其家。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou founder was garrisoning Ye and had been slandered; his entire clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Zhou founder held Ye but had been slandered, and his whole clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 永德，在潞州，聞有密詔授遇，永德探知其意，謂遇曰：“得非泣殺永德耶？

translations.literal: Yongde was at Lu Prefecture; hearing that a secret edict had been issued to Yu, Yongde discovered its intent and said to Yu: "Does this not mean you will kill Yongde with tears?"
translations.idiomatic: Yongde was at Lu when he learned that a secret edict had been issued to Yu. Guessing its intent, he said to Yu, "Are you going to have me killed?"

sentences.zh: 永德即死無怨，恐累君侯家耳。

translations.literal: If Yongde dies he will bear no resentment, but I fear bringing disaster upon your lordship's household.
translations.idiomatic: If I must die, I bear no grudge—but I fear bringing ruin upon your house.

sentences.zh: ”遇愕然曰：“何謂也？

translations.literal: Yu was startled and said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu was startled. "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: ”永德曰：“奸邪蠹政，郭公誓清君側，願且以永德屬吏，事成足以為德，不成死未晚。

translations.literal: Yongde said: "Wicked men are ruining the government; Lord Guo has sworn to purge the court. I beg that you hand Yongde over to the officials for now—if the affair succeeds it will be enough merit, and if it fails, death will not come too late."
translations.idiomatic: Yongde said, "Evil men are corrupting the government, and Lord Guo has sworn to purge the court. Hand me over to the officials for now—if he succeeds, you will have earned his gratitude; if he fails, my death will not come too late."

sentences.zh: ”遇以為然，止令壯士嚴衛，然所以饋之甚厚。

translations.literal: Yu thought this right; he only ordered stalwart men to guard Yongde strictly, yet the provisions he sent him were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Yu agreed, posting stalwart guards but sending Yongde lavish provisions.

sentences.zh: 親問之曰：“君視丈人事得成否？

translations.literal: Yu personally asked him: "Do you think my brother-in-law's affair can succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked him in private, "Do you think my brother-in-law's plan will succeed?"

sentences.zh: ”永德曰：“殆必成。

translations.literal: Yongde said: "It will almost certainly succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Yongde said, "It will almost certainly succeed."

sentences.zh: ”未幾，周祖使至，遇賀且謝曰：“老夫幾誤大事。”

translations.literal: Before long an envoy from the Zhou founder arrived; Yu congratulated him and apologized, saying: "This old man nearly ruined a great affair."
translations.idiomatic: Before long an envoy from the Zhou founder arrived. Yu congratulated him and said, "This old man nearly ruined everything."

sentences.zh: 初，魏人柴翁以經義教里中，有女，後唐莊宗時備掖庭，明宗入洛，遣出宮。

translations.literal: Earlier, a man of Wei named Chai Weng taught the classics in his neighborhood; he had a daughter who during Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong's reign served in the inner palace, and when Emperor Mingzong entered Luoyang she was sent out of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a Wei man named Chai Weng taught the classics in his neighborhood. His daughter had served in the inner palace under Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong; when Emperor Mingzong entered Luoyang, she was released from court.

sentences.zh: 柴翁夫妻往迎之，至鴻溝，遇雨甚，逾旬不能前。

translations.literal: Chai Weng and his wife went to meet her; reaching Honggou, they encountered heavy rain and for more than ten days could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Weng and his wife went to meet her, but at Honggou they were halted by heavy rains for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 女悉取裝具，計直千萬，分其半以與父母，令歸魏，曰：“兒見溝旁郵舍隊長，項黵黑為雀形者，極貴人也，願事之。

translations.literal: The daughter took all her outfit and gear, worth in total ten million cash, divided half to give to her parents, and ordered them to return to Wei, saying: "Your daughter saw beside the ditch the squad leader of a postal station—a man with a mottled black neck like a sparrow's—an extremely noble person; I wish to serve him."
translations.idiomatic: The daughter gathered all her belongings, worth ten million cash in all, gave half to her parents, and sent them back to Wei, saying, "I saw the squad leader of a postal station beside the ditch—a man with a mottled, sparrow-marked neck. He is destined for greatness, and I wish to serve him."

sentences.zh: ”問之，乃周祖也。

translations.literal: On inquiry, it turned out to be the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: When they inquired, they learned it was the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 父母大愧，然終不能奪。

translations.literal: Her parents were deeply ashamed, yet in the end they could not dissuade her.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents were deeply ashamed but could not change her mind.

sentences.zh: 他日，語周祖曰：“君貴不可言，妾有緡錢五百萬資君，時不可失。

translations.literal: Another day she said to the Zhou founder: "Your nobility is beyond words; your humble servant has five million strings of cash to supply you—the time must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: One day she told the Zhou founder, "Your destiny is beyond measure. I have five million strings of cash to give you—this moment must not be missed."

sentences.zh: ”周祖因其資，得為軍司。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder, by means of her funds, was able to become army quartermaster.
translations.idiomatic: With her funds the Zhou founder secured the post of army quartermaster.

sentences.zh: 柴翁好獨寢，人傳其能司冥間事。

translations.literal: Chai Weng liked to sleep alone; people spread word that he could manage affairs of the netherworld.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Weng preferred to sleep alone, and people said he could commune with the netherworld.

sentences.zh: 一日晨起，大笑不已，妻問之，不對。

translations.literal: One day he rose in the morning and laughed without stopping; his wife asked him, but he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: One morning he rose laughing uncontrollably; when his wife asked why, he would not say.

sentences.zh: 翁好飲，其妻逼令飲，極醉，因漏言曰：“花項漢作天子矣。

translations.literal: The old man loved drink; his wife pressed him to drink until he was thoroughly drunk, whereupon he let slip the words: "The mottled-neck fellow has become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Chai Weng loved wine, and his wife pressed him to drink until he was thoroughly drunk. Then he let slip, "The mottled-neck fellow has become emperor."

sentences.zh: ”其妻頗露之，遇亦微有聞，未深言。

translations.literal: His wife somewhat revealed this; Yu also faintly heard of it but did not speak of it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: His wife let something of it slip, and Yu caught a hint of it but said nothing further.

sentences.zh: 至是，永德故以此諷遇，遇送永德歸周祖。

translations.literal: At this point Yongde deliberately used this to hint to Yu, and Yu sent Yongde back to the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yongde deliberately alluded to this story, and Yu sent him back to the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 周祖登位，封永德妻為晉國公主，授永德左衛將軍、內殿直小底四班都知，加駙馬都尉、領和州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder ascended the throne, he enfeoffed Yongde's wife as Princess of Jin, appointed Yongde Left Guard General and chief of the fourth squad of the Inner Hall Attendants, and additionally made him Commandant of the Horse and prefect of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder took the throne, he enfeoffed Yongde's wife as Princess of Jin, made Yongde Left Guard General and chief of the fourth squad of the Inner Hall Attendants, and also Commandant of the Horse and prefect of He.

sentences.zh: 逾年，擢為殿前都虞候、領恩州團練使，俄遷殿前都指揮使、泗州防禦使，時年二十四。

translations.literal: After a year he was promoted to chief inspector of the Palace Front and regimental commissioner of En Prefecture; shortly thereafter he was transferred to commander of the Palace Front and defense commissioner of Si Prefecture, at the age of twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made chief inspector of the Palace Front and regimental commissioner of En; soon after he became commander of the Palace Front and defense commissioner of Si, at age twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，幷州劉崇引契丹來侵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande, Liu Chong of Bing Prefecture led the Khitans to invade.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiande, Liu Chong of Bingzhou led the Khitans in an invasion.

sentences.zh: 世宗親征，戰於高平，大將樊愛能、何徽方戰退衄。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong personally campaigned; they fought at Gaoping, and the great generals Fan Aineng and He Hui had just suffered defeat in battle and retreated in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong marched in person. At Gaoping the great generals Fan Aineng and He Hui had just been routed.

sentences.zh: 時太祖與永德各領牙兵二千，永德部下善左射，太祖與永德厲兵分進，大捷，降崇軍七千餘眾。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu and Yongde each led two thousand household troops; Yongde's subordinates were skilled in shooting from the left hand. Taizu and Yongde roused their troops and advanced separately, winning a great victory and accepting the surrender of more than seven thousand of Chong's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Yongde each led two thousand household troops; Yongde's men were skilled left-handed archers. They roused their forces, advanced in separate columns, won a great victory, and accepted the surrender of more than seven thousand of Chong's troops.

sentences.zh: 及駐上黨，世宗晝臥帳中，召永德語曰：“前日高平之戰，主將殊不用命，樊愛能而下，吾將案之以法。

translations.literal: When they encamped at Shangdang, Emperor Shizong lay down in his tent at midday and summoned Yongde to speak, saying: "In the battle at Gaoping the other day, the commanding generals utterly disobeyed orders—Fan Aineng and those below him—I intend to investigate them according to law."
translations.idiomatic: When they encamped at Shangdang, Shizong summoned Yongde to his midday rest in the tent and said, "At Gaoping the other day the commanders utterly disobeyed orders—Fan Aineng and the rest. I mean to punish them by law."

sentences.zh: ”永德曰：“陛下欲固守封疆則已，必欲開拓疆宇，威加四海，宜痛懲其失。

translations.literal: Yongde said: "If Your Majesty wishes only to hold fast to the borders, so be it; but if you must expand the realm and extend your authority over the four seas, you ought to punish their failure severely."
translations.idiomatic: Yongde said, "If Your Majesty only means to hold the borders, very well—but if you mean to expand the realm and extend your authority to the four seas, you must punish them severely."

sentences.zh: ”世宗擲枕於地，大呼稱善。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong threw his pillow to the ground and cried out in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong threw his pillow to the ground and cried out his approval.

sentences.zh: 翌日，誅二將以徇，軍威大振。

translations.literal: The next day the two generals were executed as a warning, and military prestige was greatly shaken into vigor.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the two generals were executed as a warning, and army discipline was restored.

sentences.zh: 進攻太原，師薄城下，永德與符彥卿、史彥超北控忻口以斷契丹援路。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Taiyuan, the army drew close beneath the city walls; Yongde, together with Fu Yanqing and Shi Yanchao, held Xinkou to the north to cut off the Khitan relief route.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced on Taiyuan and drew up beneath the walls. Yongde, Fu Yanqing, and Shi Yanchao held Xinkou to the north to block Khitan reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 太原城四十里，周師去城三百步，圍之二匝。

translations.literal: The walls of Taiyuan ran forty li; the Zhou army stood three hundred paces from the city and encircled it twice over.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan's walls ran forty li around; the Zhou army stood three hundred paces from the city and encircled it in a double ring.

sentences.zh: 自四月至六月，攻之不克。

translations.literal: From the fourth month to the sixth month they attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth month to the sixth they attacked without success.

sentences.zh: 契丹援兵果至，彥超戰沒，繼敗其眾二千，餘眾遁去。

translations.literal: Khitans reinforcements indeed arrived; Yanchao died in battle, but afterward two thousand of their troops were defeated and the remainder fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Khitans reinforcements arrived as expected. Yanchao fell in battle, but the Zhou forces then routed two thousand of the enemy and drove off the rest.

sentences.zh: 以永德領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: Yongde was made military governor of the Wuxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde was made Wuxin military governor.

sentences.zh: 師還，徙義成軍節度。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was transferred to military governor of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was transferred to the Yicheng military governorship.

sentences.zh: 時永德父穎為隸人曹澄等所害，因奔南唐。

translations.literal: At that time Yongde's father Ying was killed by the bondsman Cao Cheng and others, who then fled to Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yongde's father Ying was murdered by the bondsman Cao Cheng and others, who fled to Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 會議南征，永德請行自效，許之。

translations.literal: When a southern campaign was under discussion, Yongde requested to go and prove himself, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When a southern campaign was planned, Yongde volunteered to serve and was permitted to go.

sentences.zh: 師至壽春，劉仁瞻堅壁不下。

translations.literal: When the army reached Shouchun, Liu Renzan held fast behind his walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Shouchun, Liu Renzan held the walls and refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 永德出疲兵誘之，傍伏精騎，每戰陽不利，北退三十里，伏兵突起夾攻，大敗之，仁贍僅以身免。

translations.literal: Yongde sent out weary troops to lure the enemy, with elite cavalry hidden nearby; in each battle he feigned defeat, retreated north thirty li, then the ambush suddenly rose and attacked from both sides, inflicting a great defeat; Renzan barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde sent out weary troops as bait with elite cavalry hidden nearby. In each engagement he feigned defeat and retreated thirty li north, then his ambush rose on both flanks and routed the enemy; Renzan barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 三年，世宗親征，至壽州城下，仁贍執澄等三人檻送行在，意求緩師，詔賜永德，俾其甘心。

translations.literal: In the third year Emperor Shizong personally campaigned; reaching the walls of Shou Prefecture, Renzan sent Cao Cheng and two others in a caged cart to the imperial headquarters, intending to seek a slackening of the siege; an edict granted them to Yongde so that he might be satisfied at heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shizong marched in person. At the walls of Shouzhou, Renzan sent Cao Cheng and two others in a cage to the imperial camp, hoping to buy time; an edict granted them to Yongde so that he might have his revenge.

sentences.zh: 太祖與永德領前軍至紫金山，吳人列十八砦，戰備嚴整。

translations.literal: Taizu and Yongde led the vanguard to Purple Gold Mountain; the Wu forces arrayed eighteen forts, their battle preparations strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Yongde led the vanguard to Purple Gold Mountain, where the Wu forces had arrayed eighteen forts in tight battle order.

sentences.zh: 敵壘西偏有高隴，下瞰其營中，永德選勁弓強弩伏隴旁，太祖麾兵直攻第一砦，戰陽不勝，淮人果空砦出鬥，永德亟登隴，發伏馳入據之，敵眾散走。

translations.literal: On the western flank of the enemy fortifications was a high ridge overlooking their camp; Yongde selected strong bows and powerful crossbows and hid them beside the ridge. Taizu commanded the troops in a direct assault on the first fort; the battle feigned defeat, and the Huai men indeed emptied the fort to come out and fight. Yongde swiftly ascended the ridge, released the ambush, galloped in and seized it, and the enemy masses scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A high ridge on the western flank overlooked the enemy camp. Yongde hid strong archers and crossbowmen beside it while Taizu launched a direct assault on the first fort. Feigning defeat, they drew the Huai troops out of the fort; Yongde then seized the ridge, unleashed his ambush, and galloped in to occupy it as the enemy scattered.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又攻第二砦，鼓噪而進，始攻北門，淮人開南門而遁。

translations.literal: The next day they again attacked the second fort, advancing with drums and shouts; they began by attacking the north gate, and the Huai men opened the south gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they attacked the second fort with drums and shouts. As they assaulted the north gate, the Huai troops opened the south gate and fled.

sentences.zh: 時韓令坤在揚州。

translations.literal: At that time Han Lingkun was at Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han Lingkun was at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 復為吳人所逼，欲退師。

translations.literal: He was again pressed by Wu forces and wished to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was again pressed by Wu forces and wanted to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒，遣永德率師援之，又敗泗州軍千餘於曲溪堰，俄屯下蔡。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong was angry and dispatched Yongde to lead troops to relieve him; he again defeated more than a thousand Si Prefecture troops at Quxi Dam, and shortly thereafter encamped at Xia Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was furious and sent Yongde with reinforcements. Yongde also routed more than a thousand Sizhou troops at Quxi Dam and soon encamped at Xia Cai.

sentences.zh: 時吳人以周師在壽春攻圍日急，又恃水戰，乃大發樓船蔽江而下，泊於濠、泗，周師頗不利。

translations.literal: At that time the Wu men, because the Zhou army at Shouchun was pressing the siege daily tighter and because they relied on naval warfare, greatly launched tower ships that covered the river as they descended, mooring at Hao and Si; the Zhou army was quite disadvantaged.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu forces, seeing the Zhou siege of Shouchun tighten daily and trusting in their naval strength, launched a great fleet of tower ships that covered the river and anchored at Hao and Si, putting the Zhou army at a disadvantage.

sentences.zh: 吳將林仁肇帥眾千餘，水陸齊進，又以船數艘載薪，乘風縱火，將焚周浮梁，周人憂之。

translations.literal: The Wu general Lin Renzhao led more than a thousand troops advancing together by land and water; moreover with several ships loaded with firewood he rode the wind to set fires, intending to burn the Zhou pontoon bridge, and the Zhou men were worried.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu general Lin Renzhao led more than a thousand men in a combined land-and-water advance. He also loaded several ships with firewood and, riding the wind, set fires meant to burn the Zhou pontoon bridge, causing great alarm.

sentences.zh: 俄而風反，吳人稍卻，永德進兵敗之。

translations.literal: Before long the wind reversed; the Wu men slightly withdrew, and Yongde advanced and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the wind shifted. The Wu forces fell back slightly, and Yongde advanced and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又夜使習水者沒其船下，縻以鐵鎖，引輕舠急擊。

translations.literal: Moreover by night he sent men skilled in water to dive beneath their ships and tether them with iron chains, then drew up light boats for a swift attack.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent skilled divers beneath the enemy ships to tether them with iron chains, then sent light boats in for a swift assault.

sentences.zh: 吳人既不得進，溺者甚眾，奪其巨艦數十艘。

translations.literal: The Wu men, unable to advance, drowned in great numbers; several tens of their great warships were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to advance, many Wu soldiers drowned, and the Zhou forces captured dozens of their great warships.

sentences.zh: 永德解金帶，賞習水者。

translations.literal: Yongde removed his gold belt and rewarded the men skilled in water.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde took off his gold belt and rewarded the divers.

sentences.zh: 乃距浮梁十餘步，以鐵索千餘尺橫截長淮，又維巨木，自是備禦益堅矣。

translations.literal: Then at a distance of more than ten paces from the pontoon bridge, with iron chains more than a thousand feet long he blocked the Huai River crosswise, and also moored great timbers; from this time defenses grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: He then stretched iron chains more than a thousand feet long across the Huai River a dozen paces from the pontoon bridge and moored great timbers as well, greatly strengthening the defenses.

sentences.zh: 俄又敗千餘眾於淮北岸，獲戰船數十艘，吳人多溺死。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he again defeated more than a thousand troops on the north bank of the Huai, captured several tens of warships, and many Wu men drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he routed more than a thousand enemy troops on the north bank of the Huai, captured dozens of warships, and drowned many Wu soldiers.

sentences.zh: 詔褒美之。

translations.literal: An edict praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended his achievements.

sentences.zh: 冬，擢為殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: In winter he was promoted to overall inspector of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was promoted to overall inspector of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 四年，從克壽州還，制授檢校太尉、領鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, returning after the capture of Shouchun, he was formally appointed honorary Grand Marshal and military governor of the Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after Shouchun fell, he was made honorary Grand Marshal and Zhenning military governor.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，契丹擾邊，命永德率步騎二萬拒之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year the Khitans harassed the frontier; Yongde was ordered to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year the Khitans raided the frontier, and Yongde was ordered to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry against them.

sentences.zh: 從世宗北伐，還駐澶淵，解兵柄，加檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He accompanied Emperor Shizong on the northern campaign; on returning they encamped at Chanyuan; he was relieved of military command and given the additional titles of honorary Grand Marshal and Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Shizong on the northern campaign. On the return march they halted at Chanyuan; he was relieved of military command and made honorary Grand Marshal and Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，移忠武軍節度。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, Yongde was transferred to military governor of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, Yongde was transferred to the Zhongwu military governorship.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, Yongde was additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Yongde was also made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 永德入朝，授武勝軍節度。

translations.literal: Yongde entered court audience and was appointed military governor of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde came to court and was made Wusheng military governor.

sentences.zh: 入覲，召對後苑，道舊故，飲以巨觥，每呼駙馬不名。

translations.literal: On entering audience he was summoned for discussion in the rear garden; they spoke of old times, and he was given great goblets to drink; each time Taizu called him "Imperial Son-in-Law" without using his name.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he was summoned to the rear garden, where they reminisced over great goblets of wine and Taizu always addressed him as "Imperial Son-in-Law" rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 時幷、汾未下，太祖密訪其策。

translations.literal: At that time Bing and Fen had not yet been taken; Taizu secretly consulted him on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Bing and Fen had not yet fallen, and Taizu privately asked his counsel.

sentences.zh: 永德曰：“太原兵少而悍，加以契丹為援，未易取也。

translations.literal: Yongde said: "Taiyuan has few troops but they are fierce; moreover with Khitan support it is not easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Yongde said, "Taiyuan has few troops but they are fierce, and with Khitan support it will not be easy to take."

sentences.zh: 臣以每歲多設遊兵，擾其農事，仍發間使以諜契丹，絕其援，然後可下也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that each year you should deploy many roaming detachments to harass their agriculture, and also send secret envoys to spy on the Khitans and cut off their support—only then can it be taken.
translations.idiomatic: I suggest deploying roaming detachments each year to disrupt their farming, and sending secret agents to spy on the Khitans and cut off their support. Only then can it be taken.

sentences.zh: ”帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄歸本鎮。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he returned to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 會出師討金陵，永德以己資造戰船數十艘，運糧萬斛，自順陽沿漢水而下。

translations.literal: When troops were dispatched to campaign against Jinling, Yongde at his own expense built several tens of warships, transported ten thousand hu of grain, and descended along the Han River from Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: When an expedition was launched against Jinling, Yongde built dozens of warships at his own expense, loaded ten thousand hu of grain, and sailed down the Han River from Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 富民高進者，豪橫莫能禁，永德乃發其奸，置於法。

translations.literal: A wealthy man named Gao Jin was overbearing and none could restrain him; Yongde then exposed his crimes and punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man named Gao Jin was so overbearing that no one could restrain him; Yongde exposed his crimes and punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 進潛詣闕，誣永德緣險固置十餘砦，圖為不軌。

translations.literal: Jin secretly went to the capital and slandered Yongde, saying that along strategic terrain he had fortified more than ten forts and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Jin secretly went to court and accused Yongde of fortifying more than ten strongpoints along strategic terrain and plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 太祖命樞密都承旨曹翰領騎兵察之，詰其砦所，進曰：“張侍中誅我宗黨殆盡，希中以法，報私憤爾。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Grand Councilor of Military Affairs Chief Secretary Cao Han to lead cavalry to investigate; when asked where the forts were, Jin said: "Attendant-in-Waiting Zhang nearly exterminated my clan and kin; he hoped to use the law to repay a private grudge, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu ordered Chief Secretary Cao Han of the Bureau of Military Affairs to investigate with cavalry. When asked to identify the forts, Jin said, "Attendant Zhang nearly wiped out my clan. He only wanted to use the law to settle a private score."

sentences.zh: ”翰以進授永德，永德遽解縛就市，笞而釋之。

translations.literal: Han handed Jin over to Yongde; Yongde immediately had his bonds removed, took him to the market, flogged him, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Han turned Jin over to Yongde, who immediately had him unbound, taken to the market, flogged, and released.

sentences.zh: 時稱其長者。

translations.literal: At the time he was praised as a man of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was praised for his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年來朝，拜左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he came to court audience and was appointed Left Guard Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he came to court and was made Left Guard Senior General.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐市秦、隴竹木所過矯製免關市算，降為本衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was punished because, when marketing bamboo and timber from Qin and Long, he had wherever he passed forged edicts exempting transit duties; he was demoted to senior general of his original guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was demoted to senior general of his guard for forging edicts to evade market tolls while transporting bamboo and timber from Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 數月，復舊秩。

translations.literal: After several months his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Within months his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 六年，進封鄧國公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，連知滄、雄、定三州。

translations.literal: During the Yongxi era he successively administered Cang, Xiong, and Ding prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he served in succession as prefect of Cang, Xiong, and Ding.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，拜安化軍節度。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duan Gong he was appointed military governor of the Anhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duan Gong he was made Anhua military governor.

sentences.zh: 召還，為河北兩路排陣使，屯定州。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made battle-array commissioner of the two Hebei circuits, encamping at Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made battle-array commissioner for the two Hebei circuits, encamping at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗與契丹戰，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: He once fought the Khitans and killed and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Khitans more than once, killing and capturing a great many.

sentences.zh: 二年，丁內艱，起復。

translations.literal: In the second year he mourned his mother's death and was recalled from mourning to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he entered mourning for his mother but was recalled to duty.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，又代田重進知鎮州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he again replaced Tian Chongjin as administrator of Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chunhua he replaced Tian Chongjin as administrator of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，改泰寧軍節度兼侍中，出判幷州兼並代都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to military governor of the Taining Army and concurrently Palace Attendant, going out to administer Bing Prefecture and concurrently serve as overall deployment commander of Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Taining military governor and Palace Attendant, and sent out to administer Bingzhou as overall deployment commander of Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 永德明天文術，嘗與僚佐會食，有報遼兵寇州境者，永德用《太白萬勝訣》占之，語坐客曰：“彼雖以年月便利，乘金而來，反值歲星對逆，兵家大忌，必敗。

translations.literal: Yongde understood astronomy; once while dining with his staff, word came that Liao troops were raiding the prefectural border. Yongde divined using the Taibai Wansheng Jue and said to those seated: "Though they come riding the advantage of the year and month, advancing under the metal phase, they instead encounter the year star in opposition—an army's greatest taboo—they will certainly be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: Yongde was versed in astronomy. Once while dining with his staff, word came that Liao troops were raiding the border. He divined using the Taibai Wansheng Jue and told those present, "Though they come at an astrologically favorable moment under the metal phase, they will meet the year star in opposition—the greatest taboo in warfare. They are sure to be defeated."

sentences.zh: ”未幾，折禦卿捷報至，眾始歡伏。

translations.literal: Before long news of Zhe Yujing's victory arrived, and the assembly at last rejoiced and submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Before long news of Zhe Yujing's victory arrived, and the assembly marveled.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，契丹入邊，帝將北巡，以永德宿將，召入對便殿，賜坐，訪以邊要。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year the Khitans entered the border; the emperor was about to tour the north. Because Yongde was a veteran general, he was summoned for discussion in the informal hall, granted a seat, and consulted on frontier essentials.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year the Khitans raided the frontier. As the emperor prepared a northern tour, he summoned the veteran Yongde to the informal hall, gave him a seat, and asked his counsel on frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 以老不可從行，留為東京內外都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Because he was old and could not accompany the march, he was retained as overall patrol commissioner inside and outside the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Deemed too old to accompany the march, he was kept on as overall patrol commissioner of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，制授檢校太師、彰德軍節度、知天雄軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was formally appointed honorary Grand Preceptor, military governor of the Zhangde Army, and administrator of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made honorary Grand Preceptor, Zhangde military governor, and administrator of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 俄以衰耄，命還本鎮。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, because of age and infirmity, he was ordered to return to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, owing to age and infirmity, he was ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 是秋卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: That autumn he died, at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died that autumn at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 遣內園使馮守規護柩還京師、贈中書令。

translations.literal: The Inner Garden Commissioner Feng Shougui was dispatched to escort the coffin back to the capital; he was posthumously granted Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Garden Commissioner Feng Shougui was sent to escort the coffin to the capital, and Yongde was posthumously granted Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 諸孫遷秩者五人。

translations.literal: Five of his grandsons were promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five of his grandsons were promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 永德出母，後適安邑劉祚。

translations.literal: Yongde's birth mother, after being cast out, later married Liu Zuo of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde's birth mother, after being cast out of the household, later married Liu Zuo of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 及永德鎮南陽，祚已卒，迎母歸州廨，起二堂，與繼母劉並居。

translations.literal: When Yongde was garrisoning Nanyang, Zuo had already died; he welcomed his mother back to the prefectural offices, built two halls, and she lived together with his stepmother, Lady Liu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongde was posted at Nanyang, Zuo had already died. He brought his mother to the prefectural offices, built two halls, and housed her together with his stepmother, Lady Liu.

sentences.zh: 劉卒，馬預中參，時年八十一，太宗勞之，賜冠帔，封莒國太夫人。

translations.literal: When Lady Liu died, Lady Ma attended court audience; she was then eighty-one years old; Emperor Taizong comforted her, bestowed a cap and robe, and enfeoffed her as Grand Lady of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Liu died, Lady Ma came to court at the age of eighty-one. Emperor Taizong received her warmly, bestowed a cap and robe, and enfeoffed her as Grand Lady of Ju.

sentences.zh: 同母弟劉再思，署子城使，於市西里起大第，聚劉族。

translations.literal: His younger maternal half-brother Liu Zaishi was appointed deputy city commissioner; west of the market quarter he built a grand mansion and gathered the Liu clan there.
translations.idiomatic: His younger half-brother Liu Zaishi was appointed deputy city commissioner, built a grand mansion west of the market district, and gathered the Liu clan there.

sentences.zh: 初，永德寓睢陽，有書生鄰居臥疾，永德療之獲愈。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Yongde was lodging at Suiyang, a neighboring literatus lay ill; Yongde treated him and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Yongde was staying at Suiyang, a neighboring scholar fell ill; Yongde treated him and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 生一日就永德求汞五兩，既得，即置鼎中煮之，成中金。

translations.literal: One day the scholar came to Yongde and asked for five taels of mercury; once he obtained it, he placed it in a cauldron and boiled it, producing gold.
translations.idiomatic: One day the scholar asked Yongde for five taels of mercury. Once he had it, he boiled it in a cauldron and produced gold.

sentences.zh: 自是日與永德遊，一日，告適淮上，語永德曰：“後當相遇於彼。

translations.literal: From then on he visited Yongde daily. One day he announced that he was going to the Huai region and said to Yongde: "We shall meet again there."
translations.idiomatic: From then on he visited Yongde every day. One day he said he was going to the Huai region and told Yongde, "We shall meet again there."

sentences.zh: ”永德曰：“吳境不通，子何可去？

translations.literal: Yongde said: "The Wu territory is closed off—how can you go?"
translations.idiomatic: Yongde said, "The Wu frontier is closed—how can you go?"

sentences.zh: ”生曰：“吾自有術。

translations.literal: The scholar said: "I have my own method."
translations.idiomatic: The scholar said, "I have my own means."

sentences.zh: ”永德送行數舍，懇求藥法，生曰：“君當大貴，吾不吝此，慮損君福。

translations.literal: Yongde escorted him several li and earnestly begged for the alchemical formula. The scholar said: "You are destined for great eminence; I do not begrudge this, but I fear it would diminish your fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Yongde escorted him several li and pleaded for the alchemical formula. The scholar said, "You are destined for great eminence. I would not begrudge you this, but I fear it would diminish your fortune."

sentences.zh: ”言訖而去。

translations.literal: Having spoken, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he departed.

sentences.zh: 及永德屯下蔡，牙帳前後隊部曲八百人，皆金銀刀槊，繡旗幟。

translations.literal: When Yongde encamped at Xiacai, the eight hundred men of the vanguard and rear guard units before and behind his headquarters all bore gold- and silver-mounted halberds and spears, with embroidered banners.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongde encamped at Xiacai, the eight hundred men of his vanguard and rear guard all carried gold- and silver-mounted halberds and spears, with embroidered banners.

sentences.zh: 永德善騎射，左右分掛十的，握十矢，疾馳互發，發必中。

translations.literal: Yongde was skilled at mounted archery; ten targets were hung on either side, and grasping ten arrows he galloped swiftly, shooting in turn—every shot struck home.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde was a superb mounted archer. Ten targets were hung on either side; grasping ten arrows, he galloped past and shot in turn, never missing.

sentences.zh: 淮民環觀，有一僧睥睨，永德遽召之，乃睢陽書生也。

translations.literal: Huai commoners gathered to watch; one monk looked on with a sidelong glance, and Yongde immediately summoned him—it was the Suiyang scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Huai locals gathered to watch. One monk looked on with a sidelong glance, and Yongde immediately summoned him—it was the Suiyang scholar.

sentences.zh: 夜宿帳中，復求汞法。

translations.literal: That night he lodged in the tent and again asked for the mercury formula.
translations.idiomatic: That night he stayed in the tent and again asked for the mercury formula.

sentences.zh: 僧曰：“始語君貴，今不謬矣。

translations.literal: The monk said: "I said at the outset that you would rise high, and now that has not been mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: The monk said, "I told you at the outset that you would rise high, and now that has proved true."

sentences.zh: 終能謹節，當保五十年富貴，安用此為？

translations.literal: If to the end you can keep restraint, you will preserve fifty years of wealth and eminence—what need is there for this?
translations.idiomatic: If you remain restrained to the end, you will enjoy fifty years of wealth and eminence. What need is there for this?

sentences.zh: 然能降志禮賢，當別有授公藥法者。

translations.literal: Yet if you can humble your ambition and honor the worthy, there will be another who will teach you the alchemical formula.
translations.idiomatic: But if you can humble yourself and honor the worthy, another will teach you the alchemical formula.

sentences.zh: ”永德由此益罄家資，延致方士，故太祖以方外待之。

translations.literal: From this Yongde spent his family fortune ever more freely, inviting in Daoist adepts; therefore the Founding Emperor treated him as one outside the ordinary world.
translations.idiomatic: From this Yongde spent his family fortune ever more freely, inviting Daoist adepts, and the Founding Emperor therefore treated him as a man apart from ordinary affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，睢陽書生嘗言太祖受命之兆，以故永德潛意拱向。

translations.literal: Earlier the Suiyang scholar had spoken of the omen of the Founding Emperor receiving the Mandate; for this reason Yongde secretly inclined toward him.
translations.idiomatic: The Suiyang scholar had once spoken of the omen that the Founding Emperor would receive the Mandate, and for this reason Yongde secretly inclined toward him.

sentences.zh: 太祖將聘孝明皇后也，永德出緡錢金帛數千以助之，故盡太祖朝而恩渥不替。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was about to take Empress Xiaoming in marriage, Yongde contributed several thousand strings of cash and bolts of silk and gold to assist him; therefore throughout the Founding Emperor's reign his favor never waned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor was about to marry Empress Xiaoming, Yongde contributed thousands of strings of cash and bolts of silk and gold to assist him, and throughout the Founding Emperor's reign his favor never waned.

sentences.zh: 孫文蔚虞部員外郎，文炳殿中丞。

translations.literal: His grandson Wenwei was an outer-section member of the Ministry of Works; Wenbing was a palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Wenwei served as outer-section member of the Ministry of Works, and Wenbing as a palace censor.

sentences.zh: 王全斌

translations.literal: Wang Quanbin
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quanbin

sentences.zh: 王全斌，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Quanbin was a native of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quanbin was from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其父事莊宗，為岢嵐軍使，私畜勇士餘人，莊宗疑其有異志，召之，懼不敢行。

translations.literal: His father served Emperor Zhuangzong as commissioner of the Kelan Army and privately kept more than a hundred stalwart warriors. Emperor Zhuangzong suspected him of ulterior designs and summoned him, but he was afraid and did not dare go.
translations.idiomatic: His father served Emperor Zhuangzong as commissioner of the Kelan Army and privately kept more than a hundred stalwart warriors. When Emperor Zhuangzong suspected him of ulterior designs and summoned him, he was too afraid to go.

sentences.zh: 全斌時年十二，謂其父曰：“此蓋疑大人有他圖，願以全斌為質，必得釋。

translations.literal: Quanbin was then twelve years old and said to his father: "This must mean they suspect you of other designs. I beg to be sent as a hostage in Quanbin's place, and you will certainly be released."
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin was then twelve. He said to his father, "They must suspect you of other designs. Send me as a hostage in your place, and you will certainly be released."

sentences.zh: ”父從其計，果獲全，因以隸帳下。

translations.literal: His father followed this plan, and indeed was spared; Quanbin was therefore placed under the commander's banner.
translations.idiomatic: His father followed this plan and was indeed spared. Quanbin was then placed under the commander's banner.

sentences.zh: 宋初，李筠以潞州叛，全斌與慕容延釗由東路會大軍進討，以功拜安國軍節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, Li Yun rebelled at Lu Prefecture; Quanbin and Murong Yanzhao joined the main army advancing by the eastern route to suppress him, and for his merit Quanbin was appointed military governor of the Anguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song, when Li Yun rebelled at Luzhou, Quanbin and Murong Yanzhao joined the main army advancing by the eastern route. For his service Quanbin was made military governor of the Anguo Army.

sentences.zh: 詔令完葺西山堡砦，不逾時而就。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to complete and repair the forts and stockades of the Western Hills, and before long the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to repair the forts and stockades of the Western Hills, and the work was finished before long.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，與洺州防禦使郭進等率兵入太原境，俘數千人以歸，進克樂平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, together with Guo Jin, defense commissioner of Ming Prefecture, and others, he led troops into Taiyuan territory, captured several thousand men and returned, and advanced to take Leping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong he joined Mingzhou defense commissioner Guo Jin and others in leading troops into Taiyuan territory, captured several thousand men, and took Leping.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年冬，又為忠武軍節度。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Qiande he again became military governor of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Qiande he was again made military governor of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 即日下詔伐蜀，命全斌為西川行營前軍都部署，率禁軍步騎二萬、諸州兵萬人由鳳州路進討。

translations.literal: That same day an edict was issued to campaign against Shu; Quanbin was appointed overall deployment commander of the vanguard of the Western Sichuan field headquarters, leading twenty thousand palace infantry and cavalry and ten thousand troops from various prefectures to advance by the Feng Prefecture route.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict was issued to campaign against Shu. Quanbin was appointed overall deployment commander of the Western Sichuan vanguard, leading twenty thousand palace infantry and cavalry and ten thousand troops from various prefectures by the Fengzhou route.

sentences.zh: 召示川峽地圖，授以方略。

translations.literal: He was summoned and shown the map of the Sichuan gorges, and strategy was imparted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned, shown the map of the Sichuan gorges, and given his strategy.

sentences.zh: 十二月，率兵拔乾渠渡、萬仞燕子二砦，遂下興州，蜀刺史藍思綰退保西縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he led troops to capture the two forts of Ganqu Ford and Wanyan Swallow, then took down Xing Prefecture; the Shu prefect Lan Sizhou withdrew to hold Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he captured the forts at Ganqu Ford and Wanyan Swallow, then took Xingzhou. The Shu prefect Lan Sizhou withdrew to hold Xixian.

sentences.zh: 敗蜀軍七千人，獲軍糧四十餘萬斛。

translations.literal: He defeated seven thousand Shu troops and captured more than four hundred thousand bushels of army grain.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated seven thousand Shu troops and captured more than four hundred thousand bushels of army grain.

sentences.zh: 進拔石圌、魚關、白水二十餘砦，先鋒史延德進軍三泉，敗蜀軍靈數萬，擒招討使韓保正、副使李進，獲糧三十餘萬斛。

translations.literal: Advancing, he captured more than twenty forts including Shigu, Yuguan, and Baishui. The vanguard Shi Yande marched on Sanquan, defeated tens of thousands of Shu troops, captured pacification commissioner Han Baozheng and deputy commissioner Li Jin, and seized more than three hundred thousand bushels of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to capture more than twenty forts, including Shigu, Yuguan, and Baishui. Vanguard Shi Yande marched on Sanquan, defeated tens of thousands of Shu troops, captured pacification commissioner Han Baozheng and deputy commissioner Li Jin, and seized more than three hundred thousand bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 既而崔彥進、康延澤等逐蜀軍過三泉，遂至嘉陵，殺虜甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereafter Cui Yanjin, Kang Yanze, and others pursued the Shu army beyond Sanquan as far as Jialing, killing and capturing a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Cui Yanjin, Kang Yanze, and others pursued the Shu army beyond Sanquan to Jialing, killing and capturing a great multitude.

sentences.zh: 蜀人斷閣道，軍不能進，全斌議取羅川路以入，延澤潛謂彥進曰：“羅川路險，軍難並進，不如分兵治閣道，與大軍會於深渡。

translations.literal: The Shu people cut the plank road, and the army could not advance. Quanbin proposed taking the Luochuan route to enter. Yanze secretly said to Yanjin: "The Luochuan route is perilous and the army cannot advance together; it would be better to divide forces to repair the plank road and join the main army at Shendu."
translations.idiomatic: The Shu cut the plank road and the army could not advance. Quanbin proposed entering by the Luochuan route, but Yanze privately told Yanjin, "The Luochuan route is perilous and the army cannot advance together. It would be better to divide forces to repair the plank road and join the main army at Shendu."

sentences.zh: ”彥進以白全斌，全斌然之。

translations.literal: Yanjin reported this to Quanbin, and Quanbin approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin reported this to Quanbin, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 命彥進、延澤督治閣道，數日成，遂進擊金山砦，破小漫天砦。

translations.literal: He ordered Yanjin and Yanze to supervise repair of the plank road; within several days it was completed, and they advanced to attack Jinshan Fort and broke Xiaomantian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yanjin and Yanze to repair the plank road. Within days it was done, and they advanced to attack Jinshan Fort and broke Xiaomantian Fort.

sentences.zh: 全斌由羅川趣深渡，與彥進會。

translations.literal: Quanbin hastened by the Luochuan route to Shendu and joined Yanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin hastened by the Luochuan route to Shendu and joined Yanjin.

sentences.zh: 蜀人依江列陣以待，彥進遣張萬友等奪其橋。

translations.literal: The Shu arrayed their battle lines along the river to await them; Yanjin dispatched Zhang Wanyou and others to seize their bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu arrayed their battle lines along the river to await them. Yanjin sent Zhang Wanyou and others to seize their bridge.

sentences.zh: 會暮夜，蜀人退保大漫天砦。

translations.literal: At nightfall the Shu withdrew to hold Damantian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: At nightfall the Shu withdrew to hold Damantian Fort.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，彥進、延澤、萬友分三道擊之，蜀人悉其精銳來逆戰，又大破之，乘勝拔其砦，蜀將王審超、監軍崇渥遁去，復與三泉監軍劉延祚、大將王昭遠、趙崇韜引兵來戰，三戰三敗，追至利州北。

translations.literal: At dawn Yanjin, Yanze, and Wanyou attacked in three columns. The Shu brought out all their elite troops to meet them in battle and were again thoroughly defeated. Pressing the victory they took the fort. The Shu generals Wang Shenchao and army supervisor Chong Wo fled. Liu Yanzuo, army supervisor of Sanquan, and the great generals Wang Zhaoyuan and Zhao Chongtao again led troops to fight; three battles and three defeats followed, and the pursuit reached north of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yanjin, Yanze, and Wanyou attacked in three columns. The Shu brought out all their elite troops and were again thoroughly defeated. Pressing the victory, they took the fort. Shu generals Wang Shenchao and army supervisor Chong Wo fled. Sanquan army supervisor Liu Yanzuo and great generals Wang Zhaoyuan and Zhao Chongtao again led troops to fight; three times they were defeated, and the pursuit reached north of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 昭遠遁去，渡桔柏江，焚梁，退守劍門。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan fled, crossed the Jubai River, burned the bridge, and withdrew to hold Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan fled, crossed the Jubai River, burned the bridge, and withdrew to hold Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 遂克利州，得軍糧八十萬斛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lizhou was taken, and eight hundred thousand bushels of army grain were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou was then taken, yielding eight hundred thousand bushels of army grain.

sentences.zh: 自利州趨劍門，次益光。

translations.literal: From Lizhou they hastened toward Jianmen and halted at Yiguang.
translations.idiomatic: From Lizhou they hastened toward Jianmen and halted at Yiguang.

sentences.zh: 全斌會諸將議曰：“劍門天險，古稱‘一夫荷戈，萬夫莫前’，諸君宜各陳進取之策。

translations.literal: Quanbin convened the generals and said: "Jianmen is a heavenly barrier; the ancients called it 'one man with a spear, ten thousand men cannot advance.' Each of you should set forth a plan for taking it."
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin convened the generals and said, "Jianmen is a heavenly barrier. The ancients said, 'One man with a spear, and ten thousand men cannot advance.' Each of you should propose a plan for taking it."

sentences.zh: ”待衛軍頭向韜曰：“降卒牟進言：‘益光江東，越大山數重，有狹徑名來蘇，蜀人於江西置砦，對岸有渡，自此出劍關南二十里，至清強店，與大路合。

translations.literal: Guard commander Xiang Tao said: "A surrendered soldier named Mou Jin said: 'East of the Yiguang River, beyond several ranges of great mountains, there is a narrow path called Laisu. The Shu have placed a fort on the west bank, with a crossing on the opposite shore. From there it is twenty li south of Jianguan Pass to Qingqiang Inn, where it joins the main road.'"
translations.idiomatic: Guard commander Xiang Tao said, "A surrendered soldier named Mou Jin reported that east of the Yiguang River, beyond several mountain ranges, there is a narrow path called Laisu. The Shu have a fort on the west bank with a crossing opposite. From there it is twenty li south of Jianguan Pass to Qingqiang Inn, where the path joins the main road."

sentences.zh: 可於此進兵，即劍門不足恃也。

translations.literal: Troops can advance by this route, and then Jianmen cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Troops can advance by this route, and then Jianmen will no longer avail them."

sentences.zh: ’”全斌等即欲卷甲赴之，康延澤曰：“來蘇細徑，不須主帥親往。

translations.literal: Quanbin and the others immediately wished to roll up their armor and hasten there. Kang Yanze said: "The Laisu path is narrow; the commander-in-chief need not go in person."
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin and the others immediately wanted to march there at once. Kang Yanze said, "The Laisu path is narrow. The commander-in-chief need not go in person."

sentences.zh: 且人屢敗，並兵退守劍門，若諸帥協力進攻，命一偏將趨來蘇，若達清強，北擊劍關與大軍夾攻，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the enemy has repeatedly been defeated and gathered their troops to hold Jianmen. If the various commanders join forces in attack and one deputy general is sent toward Laisu, once he reaches Qingqiang and strikes Jianguan from the north while the main army attacks from both sides, it will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the enemy has repeatedly been defeated and withdrawn to hold Jianmen. If the commanders join in attack and one deputy general is sent toward Laisu, once he reaches Qingqiang and strikes Jianguan from the north while the main army attacks from both sides, it will surely fall.

sentences.zh: ”全斌納其策，命史延德分兵趨來蘇，造浮梁於江上，蜀人見梁成，棄砦而遁。

translations.literal: Quanbin accepted this plan and ordered Shi Yande to divide forces and hasten toward Laisu. A pontoon bridge was built on the river; when the Shu saw the bridge completed, they abandoned their fort and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin accepted this plan and ordered Shi Yande to divide forces and hasten toward Laisu. A pontoon bridge was built on the river; when the Shu saw it completed, they abandoned their fort and fled.

sentences.zh: 昭遠聞延德兵趨來蘇，至清強，即引兵退，陣於漢源坡，留其偏將守劍門。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan heard that Yande's troops were hastening toward Laisu and had reached Qingqiang; he immediately withdrew his army, formed battle lines at Hanyuan Slope, and left a deputy general to hold Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoyuan heard that Yande's troops were hastening toward Laisu and had reached Qingqiang, he withdrew, formed battle lines at Hanyuan Slope, and left a deputy general to hold Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 全斌等擊破之，昭遠、崇強，即引隻退，陣於漢源坡，留其偏將守劍門。

translations.literal: Quanbin and the others broke and defeated them; Zhaoyuan and Chong Qiang immediately withdrew, formed battle lines at Hanyuan Slope, and left a deputy general to hold Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin and the others broke and defeated them. Zhaoyuan and Chong Qiang withdrew, formed battle lines at Hanyuan Slope, and left a deputy general to hold Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 全斌等擊破之，昭遠、崇韜皆遁走，遣輕騎進獲，傳送闕下，遂克劍州，殺蜀軍萬餘人。

translations.literal: Quanbin and the others broke and defeated them; Zhaoyuan and Chongtao both fled. Light cavalry were sent forward to capture them and escort them to the court. Jian Prefecture was then taken, and more than ten thousand Shu troops were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin and the others broke and defeated them. Zhaoyuan and Chongtao both fled. Light cavalry were sent to capture them and escort them to court. Jianzhou was then taken, and more than ten thousand Shu troops were killed.

sentences.zh: 四年正月十三日，師次魏城，孟昶遣使奉表來降，全斌等入成都。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the first month of the fourth year the army halted at Weicheng; Meng Chang sent envoys bearing a submission memorial to surrender, and Quanbin and the others entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the first month of the fourth year the army halted at Weicheng. Meng Chang sent envoys with a submission memorial to surrender, and Quanbin and the others entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 旬餘，劉廷讓等始自峽路至。

translations.literal: After more than ten days Liu Tingrang and the others finally arrived by the gorge route.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days later Liu Tingrang and the others finally arrived by the gorge route.

sentences.zh: 昶饋遺廷讓等及犒師，並同全斌之至。

translations.literal: Chang's gifts to Tingrang and the others and his rewards for the army were the same as those given upon Quanbin's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's gifts to Tingrang and the others and his rewards for the army were the same as those given upon Quanbin's arrival.

sentences.zh: 及詔書頒賞，諸軍亦無差降。

translations.literal: When the edict distributing rewards was promulgated, the various armies likewise received no difference in reduction.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict distributing rewards was promulgated, the various armies received equal treatment.

sentences.zh: 由是兩路兵相嫉，蜀人亦構，主帥遂不協。

translations.literal: From this the troops of the two routes grew jealous of one another; the Shu people also sowed discord, and the commanders-in-chief therefore fell out.
translations.idiomatic: From this the troops of the two routes grew jealous of one another. The Shu also sowed discord, and the commanders fell out.

sentences.zh: 全斌等先受詔，每製置必須諸將僉議，至是，雖小事不能即決。

translations.literal: Quanbin and the others had earlier received an edict that every disposition must be jointly deliberated by all the generals; by this time even small matters could not be decided at once.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin and the others had earlier received an edict requiring every disposition to be jointly deliberated by all the generals. By this time even small matters could not be decided promptly.

sentences.zh: 俄詔發蜀兵赴闕，人給錢十千，未行者，加兩月廩食。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict ordered Shu troops dispatched to the court; each man was given ten thousand cash, and those who had not yet departed were granted two months' rations in addition.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly an edict ordered Shu troops dispatched to court. Each man was given ten thousand cash, and those who had not yet departed were granted two months' rations.

sentences.zh: 全斌等不即奉命，由是蜀軍憤怨，人人思亂。

translations.literal: Quanbin and the others did not immediately obey the order; from this the Shu troops grew resentful, and every man thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin and the others did not immediately obey the order. The Shu troops grew resentful, and every man thought of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 兩路隨軍使臣常數十百人，全斌、彥進及王仁贍等各保庇之，不令部送蜀兵，但分遣諸州牙校。

translations.literal: The military commissioners accompanying the two routes often numbered in the dozens or hundreds. Quanbin, Yanjin, Wang Renshan, and the others each protected them, not allowing them to escort the Shu troops but only dispatching prefectural adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioners accompanying the two routes often numbered in the dozens or hundreds. Quanbin, Yanjin, Wang Renshan, and the others each protected their own men, not allowing them to escort the Shu troops but only dispatching prefectural adjutants.

sentences.zh: 蜀軍至綿州果叛，劫屬邑，眾至十餘萬，自號“興國軍”。
