translations.literal: When the Shu troops reached Mian Prefecture they indeed rebelled, plundering subordinate districts; their numbers reached more than one hundred thousand, and they styled themselves the "Army for Restoring the State."
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu troops reached Mianzhou they rebelled, plundering subordinate districts. Their numbers reached more than one hundred thousand, and they styled themselves the "Army for Restoring the State."

sentences.zh: 有蜀文州刺史全師雄者，嘗為將，有威惠，士卒畏服。

translations.literal: There was one Quan Shixiong, prefect of Wen Prefecture in Shu, who had once been a general and possessed both authority and kindness; the soldiers feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: There was Quan Shixiong, prefect of Wenzhou in Shu, who had once been a general and possessed both authority and kindness. The soldiers feared and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 適以其族赴闕下。

translations.literal: He happened to be taking his clan to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He happened to be taking his clan to court.

sentences.zh: 綿州遇亂，師雄恐為所脅，乃匿其家於江曲民舍。

translations.literal: When disorder broke out at Mian Prefecture, Shixiong feared being coerced and therefore hid his family in a commoner's house by the river bend.
translations.idiomatic: When disorder broke out at Mianzhou, Shixiong feared being coerced and hid his family in a commoner's house by the river bend.

sentences.zh: 後數日為亂兵所獲，推為主帥。

translations.literal: Several days later he was seized by the mutinous troops and was made their commander.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was seized by the mutinous troops and made their commander.

sentences.zh: 全斌遣都監米光緒往招撫之，光緒盡滅師雄之族，納其愛女及橐裝。

translations.literal: Quanbin dispatched army supervisor Mi Guangxu to go and win them over by conciliation. Guangxu exterminated Shixiong's entire clan, taking his beloved daughter and his baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin sent army supervisor Mi Guangxu to win them over by conciliation. Guangxu exterminated Shixiong's entire clan and took his beloved daughter and his baggage.

sentences.zh: 師雄聞之，遂無歸志，率眾急攻綿州，為橫海指揮使劉福、龍捷指揮使田紹斌所敗；

translations.literal: When Shixiong heard this, he lost all will to submit and led his forces in a fierce attack on Mian Prefecture, but was defeated by Liu Fu, commander of the Henghai Army, and Tian Shaobin, commander of the Longjie Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shixiong heard this, he lost all will to submit and led his forces in a fierce attack on Mianzhou, but was defeated by Henghai commander Liu Fu and Longjie commander Tian Shaobin.

sentences.zh: 遂攻彭州，逐刺史王繼濤，殺都監李德榮，據其城。

translations.literal: He then attacked Peng Prefecture, drove out prefect Wang Jitao, killed army supervisor Li Derong, and seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Pengzhou, drove out prefect Wang Jitao, killed army supervisor Li Derong, and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 成都十縣皆起兵應師雄，師雄自號“興蜀大王”，開幕府，置僚屬，署節帥二十餘人，令分據灌口、導江、郫、新繁、青城等縣。

translations.literal: All ten counties of Chengdu raised troops in response to Shixiong. Shixiong styled himself "Great King for Restoring Shu," opened a headquarters, appointed staff officers, and commissioned more than twenty military governors, ordering them to hold separately the counties of Guankou, Daojiang, Pi, Xinfan, Qingcheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: All ten counties of Chengdu raised troops in response to Shixiong. He styled himself "Great King for Restoring Shu," opened a headquarters, appointed staff officers, and commissioned more than twenty military governors to hold Guankou, Daojiang, Pi, Xinfan, Qingcheng, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 彥進與張萬友、高彥暉、田欽祚同討之，為師雄所敗，彥暉戰死，欽祚僅免，賊眾益盛。

translations.literal: Yanjin, together with Zhang Wanyou, Gao Yanhui, and Tian Qinzuo, jointly campaigned against him but was defeated by Shixiong. Yanhui died in battle; Qinzuo barely escaped, and the rebel forces grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin, together with Zhang Wanyou, Gao Yanhui, and Tian Qinzuo, jointly campaigned against him but was defeated by Shixiong. Yanhui died in battle, Qinzuo barely escaped, and the rebel forces grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 全斌又遣張廷翰、張煦往擊之，不利，退入成都。

translations.literal: Quanbin again dispatched Zhang Tinghan and Zhang Xu to attack them, but they fared poorly and withdrew into Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin again sent Zhang Tinghan and Zhang Xu to attack them, but they fared poorly and withdrew into Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 師雄分兵綿、漢間，斷閣道，緣江置砦，聲言欲攻成都。

translations.literal: Shixiong divided his forces between Mian and Han, cut the plank road, placed forts along the river, and proclaimed that he intended to attack Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong divided his forces between Mian and Han, cut the plank road, placed forts along the river, and proclaimed that he intended to attack Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 自是，邛、蜀、眉、雅、東川、果、遂、渝、合、資、簡、昌、普、嘉、戎、榮、陵十七州，並隨師雄為亂。

translations.literal: From this Qiong, Shu, Mei, Ya, Dongchuan, Guo, Sui, Yu, He, Zi, Jian, Chang, Pu, Jia, Rong, Rong, and Ling—seventeen prefectures—all followed Shixiong in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: From this seventeen prefectures—Qiong, Shu, Mei, Ya, Dongchuan, Guo, Sui, Yu, He, Zi, Jian, Chang, Pu, Jia, Rong, Rong, and Ling—all followed Shixiong in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 郵傳不通者月餘，全斌等甚懼。

translations.literal: Postal relays were cut off for more than a month, and Quanbin and the others were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Postal relays were cut off for more than a month, and Quanbin and the others were greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 時城中蜀兵尚餘二萬，全斌慮其應賊，與諸將謀，誘致夾城中，盡殺之。

translations.literal: At that time there still remained twenty thousand Shu troops in the city. Quanbin feared they would join the rebels; he consulted with the generals and lured them into the space between the inner and outer walls, where they were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time twenty thousand Shu troops still remained in the city. Quanbin feared they would join the rebels. He consulted with the generals and lured them into the space between the inner and outer walls, where they were all killed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劉廷讓、曹彬破師雄之眾於新繁，俘萬餘人。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Tingrang and Cao Bin defeated Shixiong's forces at Xinfan and captured more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Tingrang and Cao Bin defeated Shixiong's forces at Xinfan and captured more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 師雄退保郫縣，全斌、仁贍又攻破之。

translations.literal: Shixiong withdrew to hold Pixian; Quanbin and Renshan again broke and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong withdrew to hold Pixian. Quanbin and Renshan again broke and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 師雄走保灌口砦。

translations.literal: Shixiong fled to hold Guankou Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong fled to hold Guankou Fort.

sentences.zh: 賊勢既衄，餘黨散保州縣。

translations.literal: Once the rebel strength had been blunted, the remaining partisans scattered to hold various prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebel strength had been blunted, the remaining partisans scattered to hold various prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 有陵州指揮使元裕者，師雄署為刺史，眾萬餘，仁贍生擒之，磔於成都市。

translations.literal: There was one Yuan Yu, commander of Ling Prefecture, whom Shixiong had appointed prefect with more than ten thousand followers. Renshan captured him alive and dismembered him at Chengdu city.
translations.idiomatic: There was Yuan Yu, commander of Lingzhou, whom Shixiong had appointed prefect with more than ten thousand followers. Renshan captured him alive and dismembered him in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 俄虎捷指揮使呂翰為主將所不禮，因殺知嘉州客省使武懷節、戰棹都監劉漢卿，與師雄黨劉澤合，眾至五萬，逐普州刺史劉楚信，殺通判劉沂及虎捷都校馮紹。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Lü Han, commander of the Hujie Army, was treated discourteously by the commanding general; he therefore killed Wu Huaijie, guest-reception commissioner of Jia Prefecture, and Liu Hanqing, director of battle boats, joined with Liu Ze, a partisan of Shixiong, and their forces reached fifty thousand. They drove out Pu Prefecture prefect Liu Chuxin and killed vice-prefect Liu Yi and Hujie adjutant Feng Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Hujie commander Lü Han was treated discourteously by the commanding general. He killed Jiazhou guest-reception commissioner Wu Huaijie and battle-boat director Liu Hanqing, joined Shixiong partisan Liu Ze, and their forces reached fifty thousand. They drove out Puzhou prefect Liu Chuxin and killed vice-prefect Liu Yi and Hujie adjutant Feng Shao.

sentences.zh: 又果州指揮使宋德威殺知州八作使王永昌及通判劉渙、都監鄭光弼，遂州牙校王可尞率州民為亂。

translations.literal: Also Song Dewei, commander of Guo Prefecture, killed prefect Wang Yongchang, the Eight Works Commissioner, vice-prefect Liu Huan, and army supervisor Zheng Guangbi; Wang Keliao, adjutant of Sui Prefecture, led the people of the prefecture in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Also Guozhou commander Song Dewei killed prefect Wang Yongchang, the Eight Works Commissioner, vice-prefect Liu Huan, and army supervisor Zheng Guangbi. Sui Prefecture adjutant Wang Keliao led the people of the prefecture in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 仁贍等討呂翰於嘉州，翰敗走入雅州。

translations.literal: Renshan and the others campaigned against Lü Han at Jia Prefecture; Han was defeated and fled into Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan and the others campaigned against Lü Han at Jiazhou. Han was defeated and fled into Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 師雄病死於金堂，推謝行本為主，羅七君為佐國令公，與賊將宋德威、唐陶鱉據銅山，旋為康延澤所破。

translations.literal: Shixiong died of illness at Jintang. They elevated Xie Xingben as leader and Luo Qijun as Assistant State Duke, and together with the rebel generals Song Dewei and Tang Taobie held Tongshan, but were soon broken by Kang Yanze.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong died of illness at Jintang. They elevated Xie Xingben as leader and Luo Qijun as Assistant State Duke. Together with rebel generals Song Dewei and Tang Taobie they held Tongshan, but were soon broken by Kang Yanze.

sentences.zh: 仁贍又敗呂翰於雅州，翰走黎州，為下所殺，棄屍水中。

translations.literal: Renshan again defeated Lü Han at Ya Prefecture; Han fled to Li Prefecture, was killed by his subordinates, and his corpse was cast into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan again defeated Lü Han at Yazhou. Han fled to Lizhou, was killed by his subordinates, and his corpse was cast into the water.

sentences.zh: 後丁德裕等分兵招輯，賊眾始息。

translations.literal: Later Ding Deyu and the others divided forces to win over and pacify them, and the rebel masses at last subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ding Deyu and the others divided forces to win over and pacify them, and the rebellion at last subsided.

sentences.zh: 全斌之入蜀也，適屬冬暮，京城大雪，太祖設氈帷於講武殿，衣紫貂裘帽以視事，忽謂左右曰：“我被服若此，體尚覺寒，念西征將衝犯霜雪，何以堪處！

translations.literal: When Quanbin entered Shu, it happened to be late winter. Heavy snow fell in the capital. The Founding Emperor set up felt curtains in the Hall for Martial Instruction, wore a purple sable fur coat and cap while conducting affairs, and suddenly said to those beside him: "Dressed like this, my body still feels cold. I think of the western campaign generals braving frost and snow—how can they endure it!"
translations.idiomatic: When Quanbin entered Shu, it was late winter. Heavy snow fell in the capital. The Founding Emperor set up felt curtains in the Hall for Martial Instruction and wore a purple sable fur coat and cap while conducting affairs. Suddenly he said to those beside him, "Dressed like this, I still feel cold. I think of the western campaign generals braving frost and snow—how can they endure it!"

sentences.zh: ”即解裘帽，遣中黃門馳賜全斌，仍諭諸將，以不遍及也。

translations.literal: He immediately removed his fur coat and cap, dispatched an inner yellow gate attendant to gallop and bestow them on Quanbin, and also instructed the various generals that he could not extend this to all.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately removed his fur coat and cap, sent an inner yellow gate attendant to gallop and bestow them on Quanbin, and told the other generals that he could not extend this to all.

sentences.zh: 全斌拜賜感泣。

translations.literal: Quanbin received the gift with bowed thanks and wept in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin received the gift with bowed thanks and wept in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 初，成都平，命參知政事呂餘慶知府事，全斌但典軍旅。

translations.literal: At first, when Chengdu was pacified, Grand Councilor Lü Yuqing was appointed to administer prefectural affairs; Quanbin was charged only with military matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu was first pacified, Grand Councilor Lü Yuqing was appointed to administer prefectural affairs while Quanbin was charged only with military matters.

sentences.zh: 全斌嘗語所親曰：“我聞古之將帥，多不能保全功名，今西蜀既平，欲稱疾東歸，庶免悔吝。

translations.literal: Quanbin once said to those close to him: "I have heard that generals and commanders of old often could not preserve their fame and merit to the end. Now that Western Shu is pacified, I wish to plead illness and return east, hoping thereby to avoid regret."
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin once told those close to him, "I have heard that generals of old often could not preserve their fame and merit to the end. Now that Western Shu is pacified, I wish to plead illness and return east, hoping thereby to avoid regret."

sentences.zh: ”或曰：“今寇盜尚多，非有詔旨，不可輕去。

translations.literal: Someone said: "Bandits and rebels are still numerous; without an edict you cannot lightly depart."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Bandits and rebels are still numerous. Without an edict you cannot lightly depart."

sentences.zh: ”全斌猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Quanbin hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 會有訴全斌及彥進破蜀日，奪民家子女玉帛不法等事，與諸將同時召還。

translations.literal: It happened that there were complaints that on the day Quanbin and Yanjin broke Shu they had unlawfully seized commoners' sons and daughters, jade, silk, and other goods; they and the generals were summoned back at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Complaints arose that on the day Quanbin and Yanjin conquered Shu they had unlawfully seized commoners' sons and daughters, jade, silk, and other goods. They and the generals were summoned back at the same time.

sentences.zh: 太祖以全斌等初立功，雖犯法，不欲辱以獄吏，但令中書問狀，全斌等具伏。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, because Quanbin and the others had first achieved merit, though they had violated the law did not wish to humiliate them with prison officers but only ordered the Secretariat to question them; Quanbin and the others fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Because Quanbin and the others had first achieved merit, the Founding Emperor, though they had violated the law, did not wish to humiliate them with prison officers but only ordered the Secretariat to question them. Quanbin and the others fully confessed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“王全斌、王仁贍、崔彥進等被堅執銳，出征全蜀，彼畏威而納款，尋馳詔以申恩。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Wang Quanbin, Wang Renshan, Cui Yanjin, and the others, bearing strong armor and sharp weapons, marched out to conquer all of Shu. The enemy feared their might and submitted; an edict was swiftly dispatched to extend grace."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Wang Quanbin, Wang Renshan, Cui Yanjin, and the others, bearing strong armor and sharp weapons, marched out to conquer all of Shu. The enemy feared their might and submitted, and an edict was swiftly dispatched to extend grace."

sentences.zh: 用示哀矜，務敦綏撫，應孟昶宗族、官吏、將卒、士民悉令安存，無或驚擾；

translations.literal: To show compassion and forbearance, and to earnestly promote pacification and reassurance, all the clansmen, officials, generals, soldiers, and common people of Meng Chang were to be kept safe and secure, with none disturbed or alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: To show compassion and earnestly promote pacification, all the clansmen, officials, generals, soldiers, and common people of Meng Chang were to be kept safe and secure, with none disturbed or alarmed.

sentences.zh: 而乃違戾約束，侵侮憲章，專殺降兵，擅開公帑，豪奪婦女，廣納貨財，斂萬民之怨嗟，致群盜之充斥。

translations.literal: Yet they violated and defied these constraints, encroached upon and insulted the statutes, executed surrendered troops on their own authority, opened the public treasury without permission, forcibly seized women, widely accepted goods and wealth, gathered the lamentations of myriad people, and brought about the flooding of bandits everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they violated these constraints, encroached upon the statutes, executed surrendered troops on their own authority, opened the public treasury without permission, forcibly seized women, widely accepted goods and wealth, gathered the people's lamentations, and brought bandits flooding everywhere.

sentences.zh: 以至再勞調發，方獲平寧。

translations.literal: It even required repeated mobilizations before peace and order were finally restored.
translations.idiomatic: It even required repeated mobilizations before peace and order were finally restored.

sentences.zh: 洎命旋歸，尚欲含忍，而銜冤之訴，日擁國門，稱其隱沒金銀、犀玉、錢帛十六萬七百餘貫。

translations.literal: When the order came to return, the court still wished to forbear, but petitions bearing grievances daily crowded the palace gates, alleging that they had concealed one hundred sixty thousand seven hundred strings of cash worth of gold, silver, rhinoceros horn, jade, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the order came to return, the court still wished to forbear, but petitions bearing grievances daily crowded the palace gates, alleging that they had concealed one hundred sixty thousand seven hundred strings' worth of gold, silver, rhinoceros horn, jade, and silk.

sentences.zh: 又擅開豐德庫，致失錢二十八萬一千餘貫。

translations.literal: They also opened the Fengde Treasury without authorization, causing the loss of more than two hundred eighty-one thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: They also opened the Fengde Treasury without authorization, causing the loss of more than two hundred eighty-one thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 遂令中書門下召與訟者質證其事。

translations.literal: The Secretariat and Chancellery were therefore ordered to summon the litigants and verify the matter face to face.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Chancellery were therefore ordered to summon the litigants and verify the matter face to face.

sentences.zh: 而全斌等皆引伏。

translations.literal: Quanbin and the others all confessed when confronted.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin and the others all confessed when confronted.

sentences.zh: 其令御史臺於朝堂集文武百官議其罪。”

translations.literal: They were ordered to have the Censorate assemble all civil and military officials in the court hall to deliberate their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: They were ordered to have the Censorate assemble all civil and military officials in the court hall to deliberate their crimes.

sentences.zh: 於是百官定議，全斌等罪當大辟，請準律處分。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officials reached a decision: Quanbin and the others' crimes warranted the death penalty, and they requested disposition according to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the officials reached a decision: Quanbin and the others' crimes warranted the death penalty, and they requested disposition according to the law.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：“有征無戰，雖舉於王師；

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "To campaign without fighting is indeed the achievement of the royal army."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "To campaign without fighting is indeed the achievement of the royal army."

sentences.zh: 禁暴戢兵，當崇於武德。

translations.literal: Restraining violence and sheathing arms should be exalted as martial virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Restraining violence and sheathing arms should be exalted as martial virtue.

sentences.zh: 蠢茲庸蜀，自敗奸謀，爰伐罪以宣威，俄望風而歸命。

translations.literal: This foolish Shu of ours defeated its own treacherous designs; we raised an army to punish crime and display might, and soon they submitted at the sight of our banners.
translations.idiomatic: This foolish Shu defeated its own treacherous designs. We raised an army to punish crime and display might, and soon they submitted at the sight of our banners.

sentences.zh: 遽令按堵，勿犯秋毫，庶德澤之涵濡，俾生聚之寧息。

translations.literal: We swiftly ordered them to settle in peace and harm not the slightest thing, hoping that nourishing grace would allow the people to live and gather in tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: We swiftly ordered them to settle in peace and harm not the slightest thing, hoping that nourishing grace would allow the people to live and gather in tranquility.

sentences.zh: 而忠武軍節度王全斌、武信軍節度崔彥進董茲銳旅，奉我成謀，既居克定之全功，宜體輯柔之深意。

translations.literal: Yet Wang Quanbin, military governor of the Zhongwu Army, and Cui Yanjin, military governor of the Wuxin Army, directed these sharp troops and carried out our settled plan. Having achieved the full merit of conquest, they should have embodied the deep intent of pacification and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhongwu military governor Wang Quanbin and Wuxin military governor Cui Yanjin directed these sharp troops and carried out our settled plan. Having achieved the full merit of conquest, they should have embodied the deep intent of pacification and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 比謂不日清謐，即時凱旋，懋賞策勳，抑有彝典。

translations.literal: We expected that within days all would be clear and calm, that they would return in timely triumph, and that lavish rewards and merit registers would follow the established canon.
translations.idiomatic: We expected that within days all would be clear and calm, that they would return in timely triumph, and that lavish rewards would follow the established canon.

sentences.zh: 而罔思寅畏，速此悔尤，貪殘無厭，殺戮非罪，稽於偃革，職爾玩兵。

translations.literal: Yet they gave no thought to reverent fear and quickly brought forth this remorse and blame: greedy and cruel without satiety, killing the innocent, delaying the sheathing of arms, and treating warfare as sport.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they gave no thought to reverent fear and quickly brought forth this remorse and blame: greedy and cruel without satiety, killing the innocent, delaying the sheathing of arms, and treating warfare as sport.

sentences.zh: 尚念前勞，特從寬貸，止停旄鉞，猶委藩宣。

translations.literal: Still mindful of their earlier labors, We specially grant leniency: only their banners and axes are suspended, yet they remain entrusted with frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Still mindful of their earlier labors, We specially grant leniency: only their banners and axes are suspended, yet they remain entrusted with frontier command.

sentences.zh: 我非無恩，爾當自省。

translations.literal: It is not that We lack grace; you should examine yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that We lack grace; you should examine yourselves.

sentences.zh: 全斌可責授崇義軍節度觀察留後，彥進可責授昭化軍節度觀察留後，特建隨州為崇義軍、金州為昭化軍以處之。

translations.literal: Quanbin may be demoted and appointed military governor and observation acting commissioner of the Chongyi Army; Yanjin may be demoted and appointed military governor and observation acting commissioner of the Zhaohua Army. Sui Prefecture is specially established as the Chongyi Army and Jin Prefecture as the Zhaohua Army to accommodate them.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin is demoted to military governor and observation acting commissioner of the Chongyi Army; Yanjin is demoted to military governor and observation acting commissioner of the Zhaohua Army. Suizhou is specially established as the Chongyi Army and Jinzhou as the Zhaohua Army to accommodate them.

sentences.zh: 仁贍責授右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Renshan is demoted and appointed great general of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan is demoted to great general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: ”開寶開，車駕幸洛陽郊祀，召全斌侍祠，以為武寧軍節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao, when the imperial carriage visited Luoyang for the suburban sacrifice, Quanbin was summoned to attend the rites and was made military governor of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaibao, when the emperor visited Luoyang for the suburban sacrifice, Quanbin was summoned to attend the rites and was made military governor of the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 謂之曰：“朕以江左未平，慮征南諸將不尊紀律，故抑卿數年，為朕立法。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "Because the lower Yangzi was not yet pacified, I feared the southern campaign generals would not respect discipline, and therefore suppressed you for several years to establish a law for Me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "Because the lower Yangzi was not yet pacified, I feared the southern campaign generals would not respect discipline, and therefore suppressed you for several years to establish a precedent."

sentences.zh: 今已克金陵，還卿節鉞。

translations.literal: Now that Jinling has been taken, I restore your banners and axes.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jinling has been taken, I restore your banners and axes.

sentences.zh: ”仍以銀器萬兩、帛萬匹、錢千萬賜之。

translations.literal: He was also bestowed ten thousand taels of silver vessels, ten thousand bolts of silk, and ten million cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was also bestowed ten thousand taels of silver vessels, ten thousand bolts of silk, and ten million cash.

sentences.zh: 全斌至鎮數月卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: Quanbin died several months after reaching his post, at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin died several months after reaching his post, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，錄其孫永昌為三班奉職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi his grandson Yongchang was enrolled as a third-rank attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxi his grandson Yongchang was enrolled as a third-rank attendant.

sentences.zh: 全斌輕財重士，不求聲譽，寬厚容眾，軍旅樂為之用。

translations.literal: Quanbin was light with wealth and valued men of talent, sought no reputation, was generous and tolerant of the multitude, and the army was glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin was generous with wealth and valued men of talent, sought no reputation, was generous and tolerant, and the army was glad to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 黜居山郡十餘年，怡然自得，識者稱之。

translations.literal: Demoted to dwell in a mountain prefecture for more than ten years, he was content and at ease; those who understood praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to dwell in a mountain prefecture for more than ten years, he was content and at ease, and those who understood praised him.

sentences.zh: 子審鈞，崇儀使、富州刺史、廣州兵馬鈐轄；

translations.literal: His son Shenjun was an honorary envoy, prefect of Fu Prefecture, and military controller of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenjun was an honorary envoy, prefect of Fuzhou, and military controller of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 審銳，供奉官、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Shenrui was an attendant official and gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: Shenrui was an attendant official and gate usher.

sentences.zh: 曾孫凱。

translations.literal: His great-grandson was Kai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson was Kai.

sentences.zh: 〈曾孫〉

translations.literal: 〈Great-grandson〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Great-grandson〉

sentences.zh: 凱

translations.literal: Kai
translations.idiomatic: Kai

sentences.zh: 凱字勝之。

translations.literal: Kai, courtesy name Shengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, courtesy name Shengzhi.

sentences.zh: 祖審鈞，嘗為永興軍駐泊都監，以擊賊死，遂家京兆。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shenjun had once been overall garrison supervisor of the Yongxing Army and died fighting bandits; the family then settled in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shenjun had once been overall garrison supervisor of the Yongxing Army and died fighting bandits. The family then settled in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 饒於財，凱散施結客，日馳獵南山下，以踐蹂民田，捕至府。

translations.literal: Wealthy in resources, Kai distributed gifts and gathered clients, daily galloping to hunt beneath the Southern Mountains and trampling the people's fields; he was arrested and brought to the prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy in resources, Kai distributed gifts and gathered clients. He daily galloped to hunt beneath the Southern Mountains, trampling the people's fields, and was arrested and brought to the prefectural offices.

sentences.zh: 時寇準守長安，見其狀貌奇之。

translations.literal: At that time Kou Zhun was defending Chang'an; seeing his appearance he found it remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kou Zhun was defending Chang'an. Seeing his appearance, he found it remarkable.

sentences.zh: 為言：“全斌取蜀有勞，而審鈞以忠義死，當錄其孤。

translations.literal: He spoke on his behalf: "Quanbin had merit in taking Shu, and Shenjun died in loyalty and righteousness; his orphan should be enrolled."
translations.idiomatic: He spoke on his behalf: "Quanbin had merit in taking Shu, and Shenjun died in loyalty and righteousness. His orphan should be enrolled."

sentences.zh: ”遂以為三班奉職、監鳳翔盩厔稅。

translations.literal: Kai was therefore appointed third-rank attendant and supervisor of the tax at Fengxiang Zhiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was therefore appointed third-rank attendant and supervisor of the tax at Fengxiang Zhiyu.

sentences.zh: 曆左右班殿直、監益州市買院、慶州合水鎮兵馬監押、監在京草場。

translations.literal: He successively served as left and right palace attendant, supervisor of the Yizhou market purchase office, military supervisor of Heshui Town in Qing Prefecture, and supervisor of the capital hay depot.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as left and right palace attendant, supervisor of the Yizhou market purchase office, military supervisor of Heshui Town in Qingzhou, and supervisor of the capital hay depot.

sentences.zh: 先是，守卒掃遺稈自入，凱禁絕，而從欲害之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the garrison soldiers swept up leftover grain stalks for their own use; Kai forbade this, and his followers wished to harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the garrison soldiers swept up leftover grain stalks for their own use. Kai forbade this, and his followers wished to harm them.

sentences.zh: 事覺，他監官皆坐故縱，凱獨得免。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, the other supervising officials were all punished for deliberate indulgence; Kai alone was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter came to light, the other supervising officials were all punished for deliberate indulgence. Kai alone was exempted.

sentences.zh: 自右侍禁、雄州兵馬監押，擢閤門祗候、定邢趙都巡檢使。

translations.literal: From right attendant guard and Xiong Prefecture military supervisor, he was promoted to gate usher and overall patrol commissioner of Ding, Xing, and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: From right attendant guard and Xiongzhou military supervisor, he was promoted to gate usher and overall patrol commissioner of Ding, Xing, and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，徙麟州都監。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he was transferred to overall supervisor of Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he was transferred to overall supervisor of Linzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗出雙烽橋、染枝谷，遇夏人，破之。

translations.literal: He once went out to Shuangfeng Bridge and Ranzhigu, encountered Tangut troops, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He once went out to Shuangfeng Bridge and Ranzhigu, encountered Tangut troops, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又破龐青、黃羅部，再戰於伺候烽，前後斬首三百餘級，獲區落馬牛、橐駝、器械以數千計。

translations.literal: He again defeated the tribes of Pang Qing and Huang Luo, fought twice at Sihou Beacon, and in all beheaded more than three hundred heads, capturing thousands of tribal horses, cattle, camels, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated the tribes of Pang Qing and Huang Luo and fought twice at Sihou Beacon. In all he beheaded more than three hundred heads and captured thousands of tribal horses, cattle, camels, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 夏人圍麟州，乘城拒鬥，晝夜三十一日，始解去。

translations.literal: The Tangut besieged Lin Prefecture; he mounted the walls to resist battle for thirty-one days and nights before the siege was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut besieged Linzhou. He mounted the walls to resist battle for thirty-one days and nights before the siege was finally lifted.

sentences.zh: 特遷西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to western-section attendant official.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to western-section attendant official.

sentences.zh: 代遷，邊寇猶鈔掠，以為內殿崇班、麟州路緣邊都巡檢使，與同巡檢張岊護糧道於青眉浪，寇猝大至，與岊相失。

translations.literal: Upon rotation he was transferred back, but frontier raiders still plundered. He was appointed inner-hall honored attendant and overall frontier patrol commissioner of the Lin Prefecture Circuit. Together with fellow patrol commissioner Zhang Bian he escorted the grain route at Qingmeilang; the raiders suddenly arrived in great force and he lost contact with Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Upon rotation he was transferred back, but frontier raiders still plundered. He was appointed inner-hall honored attendant and overall frontier patrol commissioner of the Linzhou Circuit. Together with fellow patrol commissioner Zhang Bian he escorted the grain route at Qingmeilang. The raiders suddenly arrived in great force and he lost contact with Bian.

sentences.zh: 乃分兵出其後夾擊之。

translations.literal: He therefore divided his forces, came out behind them, and attacked from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore divided his forces, came out behind them, and attacked from both sides.

sentences.zh: 復與岊合，斬首百餘級。

translations.literal: He rejoined Bian and beheaded more than one hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoined Bian and beheaded more than one hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 又入兔毛川，賊眾三萬，凱以後六千陷圍，流矢中面，鬥不解，又斬首百餘級，賊自蹂踐，死者以千數。

translations.literal: He again entered Tumao River; the rebel force numbered thirty thousand. Kai with six thousand rear troops was trapped in encirclement; a stray arrow struck his face, yet he fought without ceasing and again beheaded more than one hundred heads. The rebels trampled one another, and the dead numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He again entered Tumao River, where the rebel force numbered thirty thousand. Kai with six thousand rear troops was trapped in encirclement. A stray arrow struck his face, yet he fought without ceasing and again beheaded more than one hundred heads. The rebels trampled one another, and the dead numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 遷南作坊副使，後為幷、代州鈐轄，管勾麟府軍馬事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Southern Workshop, and later became military controller of Bing and Dai Prefectures, managing Lin and Fu army and horse affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Southern Workshop, and later became military controller of Bing and Daizhou, managing Lin and Fu army and horse affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏人二萬寇青塞堡，凱出鞋邪谷，轉戰四十里，至杜古川，大敗之，復得所掠馬牛以還。

translations.literal: Twenty thousand Tangut raided Qingsai Fort; Kai came out through Xiexie Valley, fought for forty li as far as Du Guchuan, thoroughly defeated them, and recovered the plundered horses and cattle on his return.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand Tangut raided Qingsai Fort. Kai came out through Xiexie Valley, fought for forty li as far as Du Guchuan, thoroughly defeated them, and recovered the plundered horses and cattle on his return.

sentences.zh: 經略使明鎬言凱在河外九年，有功，遂領資州刺史。

translations.literal: Frontier commissioner Ming Hao reported that Kai had served beyond the Yellow River for nine years with merit, and he was therefore appointed prefect of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commissioner Ming Hao reported that Kai had served beyond the Yellow River for nine years with merit, and he was therefore appointed prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之召還，未及見，會甘陵盜起，即命領兵赴城下。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned back; before he could be received in audience, bandits arose at Ganling and he was immediately ordered to lead troops to the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was summoned back. Before he could be received in audience, bandits arose at Ganling and he was immediately ordered to lead troops to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 賊平，拜澤州刺史、知邠州。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was appointed prefect of Ze Prefecture and administrator of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were pacified, he was appointed prefect of Zezhou and administrator of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為神龍衛四廂都指揮使、澤州團練使，曆環慶、並代、定州路副都總管，捧日天武四廂、綿州防禦使，累遷侍衛親軍步軍副都指揮使、涇州觀察使。

translations.literal: Before long he became overall commander of the four wings of the Divine Dragon Guard and regimental commissioner of Ze Prefecture; he successively served as deputy overall commander of the Huanqing, Bing-Dai, and Dingzhou Circuits, the four wings of the Sun-Upholding and Heaven-Martial Guards, defense commissioner of Mian Prefecture, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy overall commander of the palace guard infantry and observation commissioner of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became overall commander of the four wings of the Divine Dragon Guard and regimental commissioner of Zezhou. He successively served as deputy overall commander of the Huanqing, Bing-Dai, and Dingzhou Circuits, the four wings of the Sun-Upholding and Heaven-Martial Guards, defense commissioner of Mianzhou, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy overall commander of the palace guard infantry and observation commissioner of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又徙秦鳳路，辭日，帝諭以唃氏木征，交易阻絕，頗有入寇之萌，宜安靜以處之。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the Qinfeng Circuit. On the day of his farewell audience, the emperor instructed him regarding the Gus clan and Muzheng: trade had been cut off and there were signs of incursion; he should handle matters with calm.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to the Qinfeng Circuit. On the day of his farewell audience, the emperor instructed him regarding the Gus clan and Muzheng: trade had been cut off and there were signs of incursion. He should handle matters with calm.

sentences.zh: 凱至，與主帥以恩信撫接，遂復常貢。

translations.literal: When Kai arrived, he and the commanding general received them with grace and trust, and regular tribute was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Kai arrived, he and the commanding general received them with grace and trust, and regular tribute was restored.

sentences.zh: 召拜武勝軍節度觀察留後、侍衛親軍馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed military governor and observation acting commissioner of the Wusheng Army and deputy overall commander of the palace guard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed military governor and observation acting commissioner of the Wusheng Army and deputy overall commander of the palace guard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈彰武軍節度使，諡莊恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted military governor of the Zhangwu Army, with the posthumous title Zhuangke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted military governor of the Zhangwu Army, with the posthumous title Zhuangke.

sentences.zh: 凱治軍有紀律，善撫循士卒，平居與均飲食，至臨陣援枹鼓，毅然不少假。

translations.literal: Kai governed the army with discipline, was skilled at comforting and guiding soldiers, shared food and drink with them in ordinary times, yet when battle came he grasped the drum mallet with stern resolve and showed no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Kai governed the army with discipline and was skilled at comforting and guiding soldiers. In ordinary times he shared food and drink with them, yet when battle came he grasped the drum mallet with stern resolve and showed no leniency.

sentences.zh: 故士卒畏信，戰無不力，前後與敵遇，未嘗挫衄。

translations.literal: Therefore the soldiers feared and trusted him, fought with all their strength, and in successive encounters with the enemy never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the soldiers feared and trusted him, fought with all their strength, and in successive encounters with the enemy never suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 兔毛川之戰，內侍宋永誠哭於軍中，凱劾罷之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Tumao River, the inner attendant Song Yongcheng wept in the army camp; Kai impeached and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Tumao River, inner attendant Song Yongcheng wept in the army camp. Kai impeached and removed him.

sentences.zh: 尤篤好於故舊。

translations.literal: He was especially devoted and fond toward old friends.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to old friends.

sentences.zh: 子緘。

translations.literal: His son was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jian.

sentences.zh: 緘子詵，字晉卿，能詩善畫，尚蜀國長公主，官至留後。

translations.literal: Jian's son Shen, courtesy name Jinqing, was skilled at poetry and painting, married the Princess of Shu, and rose to acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Shen, courtesy name Jinqing, was skilled at poetry and painting, married the Princess of Shu, and rose to acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 康延澤

translations.literal: Kang Yanze
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yanze

sentences.zh: 康延澤，父福，晉護國軍節度兼侍中。

translations.literal: Kang Yanze's father Fu was military governor of the Huguo Army under Jin and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yanze's father Fu was Jin military governor of the Huguo Army and concurrently Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 延澤，天福中，以蔭補供奉官。

translations.literal: Yanze, during the Tianfu era, entered service by inherited privilege as an attendant official.
translations.idiomatic: Yanze, during the Tianfu era, entered service by inherited privilege as an attendant official.

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，永興李洪信入覲，遣延澤往巡檢，遷內染院副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, when Li Hongxin of Yongxing came to court audience, Yanze was dispatched to conduct an inspection and was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Inner Dyeing Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, when Li Hongxin of Yongxing came to court audience, Yanze was dispatched to conduct an inspection and was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Inner Dyeing Office.

sentences.zh: 宋初，從慕容延釗、李處耘平湖湘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, he followed Murong Yanzhao and Li Chuyun in pacifying the lakes and Xiang region.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song, he followed Murong Yanzhao and Li Chuyun in pacifying the lakes and Xiang region.

sentences.zh: 時荊南高保融卒，其子繼冲嗣領軍事，命延澤齎書幣先往撫之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Baorong of Jingnan died and his son Jichong succeeded to military affairs; Yanze was ordered to carry letters and gifts ahead to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Baorong of Jingnan died and his son Jichong succeeded to military affairs. Yanze was ordered to carry letters and gifts ahead to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 且察其情偽。

translations.literal: He was also to observe their true intentions.
translations.idiomatic: He was also to observe their true intentions.

sentences.zh: 及還，盡得其機事，因前導大軍入境，遂下荊峽。

translations.literal: Upon his return he had fully learned their secret affairs; he therefore led the main army across the border and Jing and the gorges were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return he had fully learned their secret affairs. He therefore led the main army across the border and Jing and the gorges were taken.

sentences.zh: 以勞授正使。

translations.literal: For his labors he was appointed chief commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his labors he was appointed chief commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，征蜀，為鳳州路馬軍都監，破白水、合子二砦，進擊西縣、三泉，獲韓保正。

translations.literal: During the Qiande era, in the campaign against Shu, he served as overall cavalry supervisor of the Feng Prefecture route, broke the two forts of Baishui and Hezi, advanced to attack Xixian and Sanquan, and captured Han Baozheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era, in the campaign against Shu, he served as overall cavalry supervisor of the Fengzhou route, broke the forts at Baishui and Hezi, advanced to attack Xixian and Sanquan, and captured Han Baozheng.

sentences.zh: 由來蘇路會大軍，克劍門。

translations.literal: By the Laisu route he joined the main army and captured Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: By the Laisu route he joined the main army and captured Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 及孟昶降，延澤以百騎先入成都，安撫軍民，盡封府庫而還。

translations.literal: When Meng Chang surrendered, Yanze with one hundred horsemen was first to enter Chengdu, reassured soldiers and civilians, sealed all treasuries and storehouses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Chang surrendered, Yanze with one hundred horsemen was first to enter Chengdu, reassured soldiers and civilians, sealed all treasuries and storehouses, and returned.

sentences.zh: 就命為成都府都監。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed overall supervisor of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed overall supervisor of Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會全師雄復亂，徙為普州刺史。

translations.literal: When Quan Shixiong again rebelled, he was transferred to be prefect of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Shixiong again rebelled, he was transferred to be prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 時有降兵二萬七千，諸將懼為內應，欲盡殺之。

translations.literal: At that time there were twenty-seven thousand surrendered troops; the generals feared they would serve as internal collaborators and wished to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were twenty-seven thousand surrendered troops. The generals feared they would serve as internal collaborators and wished to kill them all.

sentences.zh: 延澤請簡老幼疾病七千人釋之，餘以兵衛還，浮江而下，賊若來劫奪，即殺之未晚。

translations.literal: Yanze requested that seven thousand old, young, sick, and infirm be selected and released; the remainder would be escorted back under guard, floating down the river, and if bandits came to seize them, killing them would not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Yanze requested that seven thousand old, young, sick, and infirm be selected and released. The remainder would be escorted back under guard, floating down the river, and if bandits came to seize them, killing them would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 諸將不能用。

translations.literal: The generals would not adopt this plan.
translations.idiomatic: The generals would not adopt this plan.

sentences.zh: 俄出兵。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he marched out with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he marched out with troops.

sentences.zh: 敗賊黨劉澤三萬人。

translations.literal: He defeated thirty thousand men of the rebel partisan Liu Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated thirty thousand men of the rebel partisan Liu Ze.

sentences.zh: 復有王可尞率數郡賊兵來戰，延澤擊走之，追北至合州。

translations.literal: Again Wang Keliao led rebel troops from several prefectures to fight; Yanze struck and drove them off, pursuing north as far as He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Again Wang Keliao led rebel troops from several prefectures to fight. Yanze struck and drove them off, pursuing north as far as Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 又破可尞餘黨謝行本等，擒羅七君。

translations.literal: He again broke the remaining partisans of Keliao, including Xie Xingben, and captured Luo Qijun.
translations.idiomatic: He again broke the remaining partisans of Keliao, including Xie Xingben, and captured Luo Qijun.

sentences.zh: 事平，優詔嘉獎，就命為東川七州招安巡檢使。

translations.literal: When the affair was pacified, a special edict praised and rewarded him, and he was immediately appointed pacification and inspection commissioner of the seven prefectures of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was pacified, a special edict praised and rewarded him, and he was immediately appointed pacification and inspection commissioner of the seven prefectures of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 全斌等得罪，延澤亦坐貶唐州教練使。

translations.literal: When Quanbin and the others were punished for their crimes, Yanze was also demoted and appointed training commissioner of Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanbin and the others were punished for their crimes, Yanze was also demoted to training commissioner of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，起為供奉官，遷左藏庫副使。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he was recalled as an attendant official and transferred to deputy commissioner of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao he was recalled as an attendant official and transferred to deputy commissioner of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 坐與諸侄爭家財失官，居西洛卒。

translations.literal: He lost his office for contending over family property with his nephews, dwelt in western Luoyang, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his office for contending over family property with his nephews, dwelt in western Luoyang, and died there.

translations.literal: 〈Elder brother〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Elder brother〉

sentences.zh: 延沼

translations.literal: Yanzhao
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao

sentences.zh: 兄延沼，幼隸後唐明宗帳下。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yanzhao, in youth, served under the banner of Later Tang Emperor Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yanzhao served under the banner of Later Tang Emperor Mingzong from youth.

sentences.zh: 仕晉祖，為尚食使，改散指揮使都虞候、興聖軍都指揮使，出為隨、澤二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served Emperor Gaozu of Jin as commissioner of imperial provisions, was changed to adjutant of the scattered commanders, overall commander of the Xingsheng Army, and went out to serve as prefect of Sui and Ze Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served Jin Emperor Gaozu as commissioner of imperial provisions, became adjutant of the scattered commanders and overall commander of the Xingsheng Army, and went out to serve as prefect of Sui and Ze Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 周祖北征，延沼與白文遇、李彥崇、曹奉金並從。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned north, Yanzhao followed together with Bai Wenyu, Li Yancong, and Cao Fengjin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder campaigned north, Yanzhao followed together with Bai Wenyu, Li Yancong, and Cao Fengjin.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，為侍衛馬步軍都頭、領信州刺史。

translations.literal: During Guangshun he was chief of the palace guard horse and foot armies and concurrently prefect of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangshun he was chief of the palace guard horse and foot armies and concurrently prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征劉崇，率兵攻遼州，轉龍捷右廂都校、領岳州防禦使，真拜蔡齊鄭楚四州防禦使、晉潞二州兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong on the campaign against Liu Chong, led troops to attack Liao Prefecture, was transferred to commander of the Right Wing of the Longjie Army and concurrently defensive commissioner of Yue Prefecture, and was formally appointed defensive commissioner of Cai, Qi, Zheng, and Chu Prefectures and supervisor of troops and horses in Jin and Lu Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Shizong against Liu Chong, led troops to attack Liaozhou, was made commander of the Longjie Army's right wing and defensive commissioner of Yuezhou, and was formally appointed defensive commissioner of Cai, Qi, Zheng, and Chuzhou and military coordinator of Jin and Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，李重進叛，以延沼為前軍馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, when Li Chongjin rebelled, Yanzhao was made commander of the vanguard horse army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty, when Li Chongjin rebelled, Yanzhao was made commander of the vanguard horse army.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，改懷州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong he was changed to defensive commissioner of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 4 he was made defensive commissioner of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年，命李繼勳等征河東，以延沼為先鋒都監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiande, when Li Jixun and others were ordered to campaign against Hedong, Yanzhao was made vanguard inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 6, when Li Jixun and others were ordered to campaign against Hedong, Yanzhao was made vanguard inspector.

sentences.zh: 太祖親征太原，以延沼宿將，熟練邊事，詔領兵屯潞州，會以疾歸郡。

translations.literal: When Taizu personally campaigned against Taiyuan, because Yanzhao was a veteran general skilled in frontier affairs, he was ordered to lead troops to garrison Lu Prefecture; he happened to fall ill and returned to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor personally campaigned against Taiyuan, Yanzhao—an old general well versed in frontier affairs—was ordered to garrison Luzhou with troops, but he fell ill and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 2 he died, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 王繼濤

translations.literal: Wang Jitao
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jitao

sentences.zh: 王繼濤，河朔人，少給事漢祖左右。

translations.literal: Wang Jitao was a native of Heshuo. In youth he served at the Han founder's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jitao was from Heshuo. In youth he served at the side of the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，補供奉官，曆諸司副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was appointed attendant official and passed through deputy commissioner posts in various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianyou he was appointed attendant official and served successively as deputy commissioner in various bureaus.

sentences.zh: 仕周，為右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he was made grand general of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he was made grand general of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，為天長軍使。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, he was made commissioner of the Tianchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, he was made commissioner of the Tianchang Army.

sentences.zh: 顯德五年，遷和州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiande he was transferred to be prefect of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande 5 he was transferred to be prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，為左驍騎大將軍，再遷左神武大將軍，乾德二年，命護徒治安陵隧道。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made grand general of the Left Xiaoqi Guard, then transferred again to grand general of the Left Shenwu Guard. In the second year of Qiande he was ordered to oversee convict labor in pacifying the Anling tunnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was made grand general of the Left Xiaoqi Guard, then transferred to grand general of the Left Shenwu Guard. In Qiande 2 he was ordered to supervise convict labor on the Anling tomb tunnel.

sentences.zh: 大軍伐蜀，為鳳州路砦使。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Shu, he was made fort commissioner of the Fengzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, he was made fort commissioner of the Fengzhou route.

sentences.zh: 興元降，王全斌命繼濤權府事。

translations.literal: When Xingyuan surrendered, Wang Quanbin ordered Jitao to act on prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingyuan surrendered, Wang Quanbin ordered Jitao to administer the prefecture on a provisional basis.

sentences.zh: 孟昶降，全斌又遣繼濤與供奉官王守訥部送昶歸闕。

translations.literal: When Meng Chang surrendered, Quanbin again dispatched Jitao together with attendant official Wang Shoune to escort Chang back to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Chang surrendered, Quanbin again dispatched Jitao and attendant official Wang Shoune to escort Chang back to court.

sentences.zh: 守訥白全斌，言繼濤問昶求宮妓、金帛，全斌遂留繼濤，止令守訥送昶，俄詔以繼濤為彭州刺史。

translations.literal: Shoune informed Quanbin that Jitao had asked Chang for palace courtesans and gold and silk. Quanbin therefore kept Jitao behind and only sent Shoune to escort Chang. Shortly an edict appointed Jitao prefect of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shoune reported to Quanbin that Jitao had asked Chang for palace courtesans and gold and silk. Quanbin therefore kept Jitao behind and sent only Shoune to escort Chang. Shortly afterward an edict appointed Jitao prefect of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 綿州軍亂，劫全師雄為帥，率眾攻彭州，繼濤與都監李德榮拒之，德榮戰死，繼濤身被八槍，單騎走至成都。

translations.literal: The Mian Prefecture army mutinied, forced Quan Shixiong to be commander, and led the masses to attack Peng Prefecture. Jitao and army supervisor Li Derong resisted them. Derong died in battle, Jitao took eight spear wounds, and fled alone on horseback to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Mianzhou army mutinied, forced Quan Shixiong to serve as commander, and led the masses to attack Pengzhou. Jitao and army supervisor Li Derong resisted them. Derong fell in battle, Jitao took eight spear wounds, and fled alone on horseback to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 素與通事舍人田欽祚有隙，會欽祚入朝，乃誣奏繼濤以他事。

translations.literal: He had long had a feud with communication officer Tian Qinzuo. When Qinzuo went to court, he falsely memorialized against Jitao on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been at odds with communication officer Tian Qinzuo. When Qinzuo went to court, he falsely memorialized against Jitao on other grounds.

sentences.zh: 太祖驛召繼濤，將面質之，道病卒。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor summoned Jitao by post relay to confront him face to face, but he died of illness en route.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor summoned Jitao by post relay to confront him in person, but he died of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“故彭州刺史王繼濤，先登擊賊，身被重創，優典未加，齎志而歿。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The late Peng Prefecture prefect Wang Jitao was first to scale the walls and strike the rebels, suffered grave wounds, yet extraordinary honors had not been granted when he died bearing his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The late Pengzhou prefect Wang Jitao was first to scale the walls and strike the rebels. He suffered grave wounds, yet extraordinary honors had not been granted when he died with his grievance unredressed.

sentences.zh: 故階州刺史高彥暉，帥師討賊，奮不顧命，垂老之年，殞身鋒鏑。

translations.literal: The late Jie Prefecture prefect Gao Yanhui led troops to suppress rebels, fought without regard for his life, and in the waning years of his life perished amid spear and arrow.
translations.idiomatic: The late Jiezhou prefect Gao Yanhui led troops to suppress rebels, fought without regard for his life, and in his old age perished amid spear and arrow.

sentences.zh: 永言痛悼，不忘於懷。

translations.literal: We shall ever speak of this in grief and hold it in memory without forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: We shall ever speak of this in grief and hold it in our hearts without forgetting.

sentences.zh: 宜各賜其家粟帛。”

translations.literal: Each of their families should be granted grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Each of their families should be granted grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 高彥暉

translations.literal: Gao Yanhui
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanhui

sentences.zh: 高彥暉，薊州漁陽人。

translations.literal: Gao Yanhui was a native of Yuyang in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanhui was from Yuyang in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 仁契丹為瀛州守將。

translations.literal: He served the Khitan as garrison commander of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Khitans as garrison commander of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗北征，以城來降，遷耀、階二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned north, he surrendered with his city and was transferred to be prefect of Yao and Jie Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong campaigned north, he surrendered with his city and was transferred to be prefect of Yao and Jie Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 王師伐蜀，為歸州路先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, he was made vanguard overall commander of the Guizhou route.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, he was made vanguard overall commander of the Guizhou route.

sentences.zh: 全師雄之亂，崔彥進遣彥暉與田欽祚共討之。

translations.literal: During Quan Shixiong's rebellion, Cui Yanjin dispatched Yanhui together with Tian Qinzuo to jointly suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: During Quan Shixiong's rebellion, Cui Yanjin dispatched Yanhui and Tian Qinzuo to suppress him jointly.

sentences.zh: 至導江，與賊遇，賊據隘路，設伏竹箐中，官軍至，遇伏發，遂不利。

translations.literal: Reaching Daojiang, they met the rebels. The rebels held the narrow pass and set ambushes in bamboo thickets. When the imperial army arrived, the ambush was sprung and the battle went against them.
translations.idiomatic: At Daojiang they met the rebels. The rebels held the narrow pass and set ambushes in bamboo thickets. When the imperial army arrived, the ambush was sprung and the battle went against them.

sentences.zh: 彥暉謂欽祚曰：“賊勢張大，日將暮，請收兵，詰朝與戰。

translations.literal: Yanhui said to Qinzuo: "The rebels' force is swelling and the day is nearly spent. I ask that we withdraw the troops and fight tomorrow morning.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui said to Qinzuo, "The rebels' force is swelling and the day is nearly spent. I ask that we withdraw the troops and fight tomorrow morning.

sentences.zh: ”欽祚欲遁，慮賊曳其後，乃紿之曰：“公食厚祿，遇賊畏縮，何也？

translations.literal: Qinzuo wished to flee and feared the rebels would pull up his rear. He therefore deceived him, saying: "You enjoy rich emoluments—yet when you meet the enemy you shrink back. Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Qinzuo wished to flee and feared the rebels would pursue him from behind. He therefore deceived him, saying, "You enjoy rich emoluments, yet when you meet the enemy you shrink back. Why is this?

sentences.zh: ”彥暉復麾兵進。

translations.literal: Yanhui again waved his troops forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui again waved his troops forward.

sentences.zh: 欽祚潛遁去。

translations.literal: Qinzuo secretly fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzuo secretly fled.

sentences.zh: 彥暉獨與部下十餘騎力戰，皆死之，時年七十餘。

translations.literal: Yanhui alone, with ten-some riders under his command, fought desperately. All died. He was then in his seventies.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui alone, with a dozen or so riders under his command, fought desperately to the end. All were killed. He was then in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 彥暉老將，練習邊事，上聞其歿，甚痛惜，故並命優恤之。

translations.literal: Yanhui was an old general skilled in frontier affairs. When the emperor heard of his death, he was deeply pained and grieved; therefore he specially ordered generous consolation for both.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was an old general well versed in frontier affairs. When the emperor heard of his death, he was deeply grieved and therefore ordered generous consolation for both men together.

sentences.zh: 論曰：郭崇感激昔遇，發於垂涕。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Guo Chong, moved by past kindness, expressed it in falling tears.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Guo Chong, moved by past kindness, expressed it in tears.

sentences.zh: 太祖察其忠厚，亟焚思誨之奏。

translations.literal: Taizu perceived his loyalty and sincerity and swiftly burned Sihui's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor perceived his loyalty and sincerity and swiftly burned Chen Sihui's memorial.

sentences.zh: 雖魏文不強於楊彪，宋武無猜於徐廣，何以加之。

translations.literal: Even if Wei Wendi did not pressure Yang Biao, and Song Wudi bore no suspicion toward Xu Guang—how could one surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Wei Wendi did not pressure Yang Biao and Song Wudi bore no suspicion toward Xu Guang, how could one surpass this?

sentences.zh: 廷璋開懷以待罕孺，宋偓抗章以察重進，向拱獻謀以平上黨，乘時建功，各奮所長，有足尚者。

translations.literal: Tingzhang received Hanru with open heart; Song Wo submitted memorials to investigate Chongjin; Xiang Gong offered plans to pacify Shangdang—they seized the moment to achieve merit, each exerting his strengths. These are worthy of admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhang received Hanru with an open heart; Song Wo submitted memorials to investigate Chongjin; Xiang Gong offered plans to pacify Shangdang. They seized the moment to achieve merit, each exerting his strengths—deeds worthy of admiration.

sentences.zh: 王彥超起自戎昭，曆典藩服，引年高蹈，武夫之貞；

translations.literal: Wang Yanchao rose from military service, successively governed feudal commands, cited age and withdrew to lofty retirement—the steadfastness of a warrior;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao rose from military service, successively governed frontier commands, cited age and withdrew to retirement—the steadfastness of a warrior;

sentences.zh: 至於自悔多殺，垂戒後裔，近乎仁人之用心。

translations.literal: As for regretting his many killings and leaving warnings for his descendants, this approaches the mind of a benevolent man.
translations.idiomatic: As for regretting his many killings and leaving warnings for his descendants, this approaches the mind of a benevolent man.

sentences.zh: 張永德前朝勳伐，夙識太祖，潛懷尊奉，雖有橋公祖之知，而非人臣之不二心者矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde was a meritorious minister of the previous dynasty who had known the Founding Emperor from early on and secretly harbored reverence for him. Though he had the discerning eye of Qiao Gongzu, he was not a minister of single-hearted loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde was a meritorious minister of the previous dynasty who had known the Founding Emperor from early on and secretly harbored reverence for him. Though he had the discerning eye of Qiao Gongzu, he was not a minister of undivided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 乾德伐蜀之師，未七旬而降款至，諸將之功，何可泯也。

translations.literal: The army that campaigned against Shu in Qiande, within seventy days brought surrender—how can the generals' merit be erased?
translations.idiomatic: The army that campaigned against Shu in Qiande brought surrender within seventy days. How can the generals' merit be erased?

sentences.zh: 王全斌黷貨殺降，尋啟禍變，太祖罪之，而從八議之貸，斯得馭功臣之道。

translations.literal: Wang Quanbin coveted goods and killed those who surrendered, soon bringing calamity and rebellion. Taizu punished him, yet granted the commutation of the Eight Deliberations—this is the way to manage meritorious subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quanbin coveted goods and killed those who surrendered, soon bringing calamity and rebellion. The Founding Emperor punished him yet granted the commutation under the Eight Deliberations—this is the way to manage meritorious subjects.

sentences.zh: 延澤能相地險，豫謀屯備。

translations.literal: Yanze could read terrain dangers and plan defenses in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yanze could read terrain dangers and plan defenses in advance.

sentences.zh: 繼濤、彥暉，先登重傷，殞沒無避，咸可稱焉。

translations.literal: Jitao and Yanhui, first to advance and gravely wounded, died without flinching—all are praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao and Yanhui, first to advance and gravely wounded, died without flinching—all are worthy of praise.
